final.architecture:
SEEN AT WESTSIDE is one magazine with 311 addresses. Its line is 'Every look has an address.' We sell it as Westside's own Indian calendar (seasons, thresholds, wedding cards, families), made with Zara-grade restraint and measured at Westside's own counters. We never position it as 'Zara at Westside prices'.

THREE RULES FOR EVERY ASSET
1. It carries a number and a dateline, e.g. 'WINDOW No. 047 · SEEN AT WESTSIDE, <STORE>, <CITY>'.
2. It ends in one store action, sent to that store's WhatsApp with a property code: BOOK (a stylist, a trial room or a portrait), HOLD (your size until Sunday close) or RSVP (a guest list).
3. The billing counter captures the WestStyleClub ID together with the code. That links post, booking, visit and bill for each store.

EIGHT PROPERTIES IN FIVE ROLES
- SPINE: MAUSAM. Four numbered issues a year on India's seasons: Garmi (Mar), Baarish (Jul), Tyohaar (Oct-Nov) and Shaadi (Nov). Only Garmi and Baarish are standalone shoots. Tyohaar is Dehleez and Shaadi is Five Functions, so the spine adds no second production machine. Each issue sets the three colours every property uses that quarter.
- WEEKLY: THE WINDOW and THE TRIAL ROOM.
  - The Window (Friday): one bay and one look in each of the 311 stores, with a Window rail just inside the door.
  - The Trial Room (Wednesday episode, plus fortnightly bylined columns): Style Call is its booking step.
- MONTHLY: SEEN IN. A pavement studio outside one store in each city. The prints hang inside the store the next week, and the shoot is also the casting engine for the other properties.
- ROLLING: FIRST LOOK, at every opening. New cities, flagships and new formats get the full tier; infill stores get a kit.
- DATED: DEHLEEZ (Navratri to Bhai Dooj, from Diwali 2027) and FIVE FUNCTIONS (Nov-Feb, piloted on the Jan-Feb 2027 wedding dates).
- ENGINE: THE REGULARS. One creator ladder on WestStyleClub IDs. It absorbs the Style Collective, YNG, FRONT ROW, Wesness captains (as the Runner track, which replaces Start Line) and The Bench humour brief (which replaces Just Looking).

MECHANICS, NOT PROPERTIES
- Style Call: a 15-minute WhatsApp video call that converts to a held trial room.
- HOLD and RSVP.
- The 72-hour Burst: local Regulars, city pages, PR and geo-paid media within 5-8 km of the named store, after every opening, Mausam issue and Five Functions premiere.

CHANNELS
- @westside, kept quiet like a magazine.
- The Westside app and site.
- WestStyleClub WhatsApp.
- 311 windows and thresholds.
- Each store's Google Business Profile.
Creators post on their own handles, tagged to a store. There is no new handle.

WEEKLY RHYTHM
- Mon: column.
- Wed: Trial Room episode.
- Thu: column, plus the members' Window preview at night.
- Fri: Window.
- Sun: Seen In (monthly in each city).

GLASS CALENDAR (52 weeks, written now)
- Each store has one Window bay, and that bay carries one programme a week.
- In a Mausam launch week, that week's Window is the issue cover.
- In Dehleez weeks the threshold carries the festive moment and the bay stays clean.
- First Look objects go only in that store's bay.
- No two programmes ever share the same glass.

WEIGHTING
Window, Trial Room, Seen In, Dehleez and Five Functions all work on the roughly 300 mature stores, where like-for-like growth is low single digits. First Look covers the new stores.

MEASUREMENT
- The KPI spine runs in this order: footfall per store, then BOOK/HOLD/RSVP per store, then member-attributed bills, then average bill against walk-ins.
- Every national rollout installs in two waves a week apart, so each one carries its own control group.
- Each test store gets 3-5 matched control stores, or a synthetic control built from the network.
- Festive and wedding results are read like-for-like, year on year.
- One store can only detect a lift of about 10% or more over 4-6 weeks. Reads therefore pool the city cluster, and 'inconclusive' is defined before launch.
- Record Diwali 2026 and the 2026-27 wedding season per store now, as baselines.

PILOT: ONE STORE, EIGHT WEEKS
- Recommended: the next Q4 FY27 opening (Jan-Mar 2027) runs as First Look and carries Window No. 001, The Trial Room (four stylists across the store and its cluster) and Seen In.
  - The new store is read against the opening curve of comparable Q4 FY26 openings.
  - The cluster stores are read against matched controls.
- Festive-drop alternative: Five Functions with Bring the Card in one existing store, on the Jan-Feb 2027 wedding dates.
- Nothing is attempted for Diwali 2026 (8 Nov) beyond recording baselines.
- After the pilot:
  - Mausam No. 01 Garmi (Mar 2027), when The Window goes national.
  - Dehleez Edition 01 (Diwali 2027, artist announced Aug 2027).
  - Five Functions Edition 02, nationwide (Nov 2027).

PRODUCTION CAP
- Weekly: one Window still and loop, and one Trial Room episode.
- Fortnightly: the columns.
- Monthly: Seen In in each city, and one Regulars brief.
- Quarterly: Mausam stills.
- Per opening: a kit.
- Two films per Mausam year: the Baarish film and the Five Functions series.
- Not in year one: serials, label films, routine livestreams or certified races.

CUT OR FOLDED
- Roshni goes into Dehleez.
- The Serial's film rules go into Five Functions.
- Dateline goes into the Trial Room columns.
- Style Call stays only as a booking mechanic; the property and its Log film are cut.
- Start Line goes into The Regulars and First Look.
- Cut outright: The Function, Editions, the @seenatwestside handle, 3-day premieres at every opening, quarterly Mausam films and a separate Mausam cover install.

PARKED
Re-Edition: one archive volume a year, Aug 2027 at the earliest. It goes ahead only if archive prints, patterns and deadstock exist and Westside's founding year is confirmed.

ips.name: MAUSAM (मौसम)
ips.line: India's real seasons as four numbered issues a year. Each issue has one house crew, three declared colours and one cover that runs on every Westside surface.
ips.role: Spine. It sets each quarter's palette, cast and cover. Garmi and Baarish are standalone shoots. Tyohaar is Dehleez and Shaadi is Five Functions, so the frame adds no second production machine.
ips.precedent: Zara Studio Collection. It was introduced as a premium capsule for fall 2016. In the seasons documented from SS22 to SS26, a stable core crew shoots it: Steven Meisel, Baron & Baron/Fabien Baron, Karl Templer, Pat McGrath and Guido Palau. The film genre changes each season and the palette is declared (SS26: powder blue, sage, blush). Zara also renews its windows with each campaign. We borrow the fixed crew, the declared palette and the changing genre. India's four seasons are ground that Zara's SS/FW calendar does not cover. We do not claim the 'same team since 2016'. 'No price on the image' is our reading of campaign coverage, not an audit.
ips.cadence:
Quarterly, numbered from Mausam No. 01:
- No. 01 GARMI: first week of March 2027.
- No. 02 BAARISH: first week of July 2027.
- No. 03 TYOHAAR: Dehleez Edition 01, Navratri to Bhai Dooj 2027.
- No. 04 SHAADI: Five Functions Edition 02, mid-November 2027.
The cover goes up in two waves a week apart.
ips.channels: A run of 6-9 frames on the @westside grid with little or no caption; the app and westside.com home and issue page; the WestStyleClub WhatsApp header; The Window bay in issue week (wave A, then wave B); the cash-desk card; OOH only around that quarter's openings.
ips.cast: 8-10 faces per issue, drawn from FRONT ROW's 30 New Faces, Seen In discoveries and two Westside store staff. Every issue includes at least one sitter over 50 and spans regions and sizes. Umashan Naidoo is house creative director, with one external photographer, stylist and art director held for at least four issues. Beauty is by Studiowest, credited.
art_direction: Shoot one real Indian location per issue as architecture, with no added props. Garmi: a Chandigarh-style brutalist corridor at noon. Baarish: a Mumbai stairwell in real rain.
Use daylight from one direction and keep the shadows. Shoot Baarish only in real overcast weather, never in a studio.
Put one figure in each frame, full-length or three-quarter at 3:4 and 9:16, with headroom. Never cut at the hem, and never put product grids on the cover.
Declare three named colours on the cover (e.g. Baarish: slate, moss, wet sand). Reuse them on window planes, the trial-room wall, signage, the WhatsApp header and the film grade.

Put Westside's own wordmark top left, with 'MAUSAM No. 02 / BAARISH' beneath it in small uppercase sans and the numeral in the serif. A hairline Devanagari मौसम is the second mark; city cuts carry the city's script.
Put no price, offer or call to action on any image, and give every post full magazine credits.
ips.store_hook: In issue week the cover is that week's Window. It goes into wave A stores first and wave B stores a week later. The app's issue page shows each look in stock at the member's home store. The code on the cash-desk card books a 30-minute Mausam fitting (BOOK) or holds a size (HOLD) at that store.
ips.kpi: Issue-week footfall per store, wave A against wave B stores that do not yet have the cover, and like-for-like against the same weeks last year. We do not compare with the previous four weeks, because seasonality confounds that comparison. Also: Mausam fittings booked and attended per store, and 14-day sell-through of the cover looks per store.
episode_examples: Mausam No. 01 / GARMI: 'Linen Hours' (one Chandigarh corridor at noon: bone, khaki, indigo)
Mausam No. 02 / BAARISH: 'Slate, Moss, Wet Sand' (a silent 60-second film in one Mumbai stairwell, one of the year's two films)
Mausam No. 03 / TYOHAAR: Dehleez Edition 01 (Diwali 2027)
Mausam No. 04 / SHAADI: Five Functions Edition 02 (November 2027)
ips.hero_visual: A woman in a slate Utsa kurta stands three-quarter length on a rain-dark Mumbai stairwell in flat grey daylight. The only graphics are Westside's own wordmark top left, 'MAUSAM No. 02 / BAARISH' in small capitals beneath it, and a hairline मौसम.

ips.name: THE WINDOW
ips.line: Every Friday one numbered look goes into one window bay in every Westside and onto every Westside screen the same morning. The full look waits on a rail just inside the door.
ips.role: The always-on weekly cover and newness signal, on the most-seen surface Westside owns. It is built to lift footfall in the roughly 300 mature stores, not only at openings, and every installation doubles as a test.
ips.precedent: For the numbering we borrow from Zara SRPLS. It runs as numbered collections from CLLCTN 02 (Spring 2019) to CLLCTN 16 (Apr 2026), under one credited creative director (Karl Templer) and a recurring photographer (Craig McDean). SRPLS is twice-yearly, not weekly. Zara also renews its windows with each campaign, and it mocks up stores and windows centrally in full-scale pilot stores at A Coruña (Business Insider, 2018). The weekly cadence is Westside's own. Its AI design suite produces 400-500 designs a week (Bloomberg / Retail Insight Network, Jul 2026); no Zara practice supports a weekly window. That a numbered run becomes 'collectible' is an inference, not a documented result.
ips.cadence: Weekly, at store opening on Friday. Numbered continuously from Window No. 001, so 52 a year, gathered each quarter into a nine-frame grid. The national install runs in two waves a week apart. In a Mausam launch week the Window is the issue cover. In Dehleez weeks the bay stays clean.
ips.channels: The 311 window bays; the @westside grid (one frame, with the hero store rotating across cities) and Stories; an app home tile; the WestStyleClub Friday WhatsApp message; each store's Google Business Profile photo, updated the same morning; window screens in flagships looping the 6-second film.
ips.cast: Mannequins only. Westside's visual-merchandising head is credited as the series' creative director for a year. One house photographer shoots the reference window. Each store's VM lead is credited 'Dressed by' on the local version.
art_direction: One look from one label, on at most three mannequins. Every form is fully dressed: drape, bag, footwear, jewellery.
The backdrop is the current Mausam colours as flat plaster or paper planes, and nothing else. No SALE vinyl, festoons or props ever touch the bay.
The number is the only graphic on the glass: 'No. 047' in the house serif, about 30 cm high, bottom left.
Photograph straight on at mannequin eye height at 07:00, before the mall opens, at 3:4. Use the same angle in the same reference store every week, so the archive reads as one grid.
Light it with warm 3000K top light plus one side wash. Street reflections in the glass are allowed; gels and LED chasers are not.
ips.store_hook: The full look, in all sizes, sits on a Window rail just inside the door for seven days. Members get the photo on Thursday night. Replying 'HOLD 047' to their own store's WhatsApp, or scanning the rail card, holds their size until Sunday close.

Window No. 014: 'First Rain' (Nuon raincoats in slate)
Window No. 032: 'Three Cousins, One Sangeet' (Vark)
ips.hero_visual: A three-by-three grid of Friday windows shot straight on from the mall floor. Each is a single look on a flat colour plane, numbered No. 001 to No. 009 in tall serif numerals on the glass. The screen opens full-bleed on No. 001: one E.T.A. trench against slate at 07:00, with the wet street reflected in the glass.

ips.name: THE TRIAL ROOM
ips.line: A store stylist, a real member and one brief, filmed through the curtain of a named store's trial room. Every episode and column ends in 'Book <stylist> at <store>'.
ips.role: The one conversion path, made of a weekly episode and fortnightly bylined columns. Style Call is its booking mechanic, not a separate property: a 15-minute WhatsApp video call that converts to a held trial room. Dateline is folded in as the column headline.
ips.precedent: Zara's The Fold-er (12 Jun 2026) runs four bylined columns inside zara.com and the app, each illustrated with the author's own photos and a shop link under every image. Zara's Nanjing flagship opened a 'fit check' studio on 21 Mar 2025, with brand-controlled cameras and light, booked through WeChat. Zara Try-On passed 7M sessions by 11 Mar 2026 (Inditex), which shows that 'will it suit me' drives use. Westside answers that question with a person in a store. We do not cite Store Mode's fitting-room booking as a current feature, because it is documented only in 2020-23 coverage.
ips.format:
The weekly episode is a 45-60 second vertical film plus a 5-frame carousel. The member arrives with a brief, the stylist passes three looks through the curtain, and the member chooses at the mirror.

The column runs fortnightly from each bylined stylist. It has 250-300 words under a city-dateline headline ('DATELINE: KORAMANGALA, BENGALURU') and 6-8 phone portraits shot to house rules, with live stock at that store under every image.

Both end in BOOK: a held 30-minute trial room with sizes pulled, or a 15-minute Style Call first.
ips.cadence: Episodes run weekly on Wednesdays, numbered in seasons of 12 from Trial Room No. 001. Columns run fortnightly. The pilot has 4 stylists in 4 stores: the pilot store and three in its cluster. Year one has 30-50 stylists, one per new-format store, and no more until quality holds. Columns are collected each quarter as 'The Trial Room, Vol. 0X'. Briefs rotate monthly: office, monsoon, college, festive, wedding guest.
ips.channels: @westside Reels and Shorts; a named Trial Room section in the app and on the site; WestStyleClub WhatsApp, where the episode arrives with a BOOK button; collab posts with the stylist's own handle; screens beside the trial rooms.
ips.cast: Westside store stylists (the Style Collective), bylined with their home store. Real WestStyleClub members, cast through a 'cast me' WhatsApp call, paid and with signed releases. Store staff appear as themselves. YNG creators host the college season and write one guest column per Mausam issue.
art_direction: The curtain is the frame. Shoot from outside the room with the curtain half drawn: a sliver of mirror, a hand passing a hanger. Show full length only on the reveal.

Pilot and new-format stores share one house room spec: one hook, one stool, a full-length mirror, a wall in the Mausam colour, and a warm 3000-3200K panel in place of the tube light. The room number is stencilled on the door.
Shoot on a fixed phone rig at chest height, never a handheld selfie. The stylist directs and the rig shoots.
Cast real members of any age and size, never models. Studiowest make-up stays natural, with no beauty filters. Faces may be cropped for privacy.

Bylines read 'THE TRIAL ROOM No. 012 / BY <NAME>, WESTSIDE <STORE>, <CITY>'. The essay is in sentence case and product names in small capitals. Prices appear only in the shop edit, never on a portrait or in the film.
Sound is room tone and the curtain rail. The Mausam track plays only on the reveal.
ips.store_hook: Message 'BOOK 012' to that store's WhatsApp. The stylist pulls the episode's three looks in your size and holds that trial room for 30 minutes on a day you choose, and you can bring a friend. Each store publishes its open slots every week and replies within an agreed booking SLA.
episode_examples: Trial Room No. 001: 'My brother's sangeet, and no lehenga'
Trial Room No. 004: 'Client pitch on Monday' (Wardrobe)
The Trial Room, column No. 07, Dateline: Bandra, Mumbai: 'One raincoat, five monsoon commutes'
ips.hero_visual: A half-drawn ivory curtain, and a hand passing a Utsa kurta through the gap. In the sliver of mirror, a woman in her forties is laughing. The door is stencilled 'TRIAL ROOM 4 · WESTSIDE <STORE>', with a small byline in the corner.

ips.name: SEEN IN
ips.line: Once a month in each city, a white seamless goes up on the pavement outside one Westside and the neighbourhood is photographed in its own clothes. The prints hang in that store the next week, and the subjects collect them there.
ips.role: Always on, monthly in each city. It is the cheapest beautiful property in the set and a footfall lever for mature stores. It is also the casting engine for Mausam, First Look and The Regulars.
ips.precedent: This is Westside's own format. No Zara or Target precedent is claimed for street casting. The look alone borrows from Zara Studio SS25 'On the Road': rough black-and-white studio portraits referencing Avedon's In the American West, cast with models, not people from the street.
ips.format: 12-20 full-length portraits on a 2.4 m seamless, plus a 30-second 'what are you wearing and why' voice clip, a carousel and a Reel. The following week a printed portrait wall goes up at the host store's entrance.
ips.cadence: Monthly in each city: shot on a Saturday afternoon and published that Sunday. Festival specials: Durga Puja (Kolkata), Ganesh Chaturthi (Pune, Mumbai) and Bihu (Guwahati). It also runs on opening day at every full-tier First Look.
ips.channels: @westside carousels and Reels; the app; city-segmented WestStyleClub WhatsApp; the host store's entrance wall.
ips.cast: Passers-by and shoppers in their own clothes, across generations. Local Regulars act as street-casting scouts. The house photographer shoots it, or a trained YNG photographer working to the same spec. Everyone signs a release, and minors need guardian consent.
art_direction: Put a 2.4 m chalk-white seamless on the pavement in open shade and use daylight only. Keep the street and the Westside fascia visible at the edges, so the address is in every frame.
Shoot full length and centred, with the same focal length and camera height every month in every city, so the archive reads as one.
Make the cover frame black and white; the carousel is in colour.
Caption formula: first name, age, neighbourhood and one quote, with honest credits for everything worn, including non-Westside pieces ('Saree from my nani, jacket from Westside').
Every set includes at least one person over 55 and one teen or child, because Westside is a family store.
ips.store_hook: The prints go up in the host store a week later ('SEEN IN SALT LAKE, 17 OCT'). Each subject collects a framed print at the billing counter with an RSVP code and gets a WestStyleClub invite. Subjects usually bring the family to see the wall.
ips.kpi: Host-store footfall in the week the wall goes up, against matched control stores in the same city. Also: prints collected, new WestStyleClub sign-ups at collection, and family group size on collection visits.

Seen In: Koramangala, Saturday 4pm
Seen In: Opening day, First Look No. 312
ips.hero_visual: A black-and-white full-length portrait of a 68-year-old Kolkata grandmother in her own handloom saree and a Westside denim jacket. She stands on a white seamless on a crowded Puja-week pavement, with the edge of the Westside fascia just in frame.

ips.name: FIRST LOOK
ips.line: Every new Westside opens as a numbered premiere: a preview night for its pin codes, one local maker's object alone in the window, and the store team as the masthead. Return visits are built in.
ips.role: Rolling, with the openings, which arrive in clusters: guidance is about 50 a year, with up to 100 discussed. It is the pilot vehicle. It has two tiers: the full programme for new cities, flagships and new formats, and a kit for infill stores. Start Line's opening run and Seen In's opening-day shoot are folded in.
ips.precedent: Zara premieres collections, not stores; what we borrow is the room. Re{form} Zara by John Galliano Vol. 1 was shown by appointment, booked through zara.com, in a Marais hôtel particulier (1-6 Oct 2026). Bad Bunny's collection was previewed at a hometown pop-up in Plaza Las Américas (16 May 2026) before the global drop. The 50 Creators pop-up at 40 avenue George V (2-5 Oct 2025) added talks and a café. Numbering by store count follows Trent's own habit of numbered store-launch releases, such as its 243rd Westside store.
ips.format:
FULL TIER
- A preview night the evening before opening: 250-400 RSVPs by pin code on WhatsApp, a local FRONT ROW host and city press.
- A commissioned local maker's object alone in the window for the opening month.
- The store team photographed as the store's masthead.
- Window No. 001 for that store.
- A Seen In shoot at the door on day one.
- A Wesness run ending at the store on the first Saturday.
- The 72-hour Burst within 5-8 km.
- An app livestream for new cities only.

KIT TIER
Preview night, window object, entrance portraits and the 72-hour Burst.
ips.cadence: Every opening. Each is numbered by Westside's store count once the rule is settled with Trent (e.g. First Look No. 312, given 311 open on 30 Sep 2026). Crew capacity is planned for clusters of 20 or more openings a quarter: Q4 FY26 had 23 openings, Q1 FY27 had 1 net addition and Q2 FY27 had 10.
ips.channels: A countdown on the hoarding; WestStyleClub WhatsApp to members in the catchment; geo-paid Instagram and YouTube within 5-8 km; local creators and city pages; city press; one frame on the national grid.
ips.cast: The new store's team, introduced by name; WestStyleClub members by pin code; a new local cohort of 3-5 Regulars; one FRONT ROW culture-shaper from the city as host; one local maker or craft cluster; the city's Wesness chapter where one exists.
art_direction: The store number is the logo of the week: 'No. 312' in the house serif on the hoarding, invitation, bag sticker and first post, with the city name in its own script beneath.
The hoarding is the teaser: plain uppercase lines only ('No. 312. OPENS FRIDAY. <AREA>.'), with no renders and no faces.
Shoot the store empty and fully lit the night before, as one dead-symmetrical frame from the entrance, with the team lined up between the rails as the cast photograph.
One local object stands alone in the window with no product beside it: bidri in Hyderabad, kantha in Kolkata, cane and bamboo in the north-east. No balloon arches, ribbon or 'Grand Opening'.
Shoot portraits of the first 30 customers at the entrance on a seamless in the current Mausam colour, with the same lens, height and distance at every opening, so the openings build one archive.
The invitation is a letterpress card with the store number and address, mirrored exactly in the WhatsApp invite.
ips.store_hook: Members RSVP for the preview night by pin code, and can book 'first hour' trial-room slots before the doors open. Portraits of the first 30 customers are printed and handed over when the sitters come back a week later. Every guest also leaves with a numbered card for a first Style Call within 30 days.
episode_examples: First Look No. 312: 'Bidri', Westside <area>, Hyderabad (full tier; store and number to confirm)
First Look No. 318: an infill store in Gurugram, kit tier (preview night, cane-and-brass window object, entrance portraits)
First Look: Westside's first store in a new city, the one opening with a livestream that quarter
ips.hero_visual: A new Westside shot dead centre from the entrance the night before opening. The floor is empty and fully lit, and the whole team stands in a line between the rails like a cast photograph. A single bidri-inlaid object stands alone in the window, with 'FIRST LOOK No. 312' small at the top.

ips.name: DEHLEEZ (दहलीज़)
ips.line: Every Diwali one named Indian artist designs the threshold of every Westside, and families book a free portrait standing on it in their festive best.
ips.role: The annual festive tentpole and the Mausam Tyohaar issue, running Navratri to Bhai Dooj. It spreads the festive moment across all 311 doors instead of concentrating it in one flagship. Roshni's artist, colour and light rules are folded in.
ips.precedent: Zara x Jayesh Sachdev 'Reverie' (15 Oct 2024) was Zara's first India collaboration: a Diwali artist capsule anchored by one 10-ft tiger sculpture at Phoenix Palladium, Mumbai, with corners in four more cities. Our search found no 2025 sequel. That is a negative search, not proof, and Zara India ran a local 'Curated At Home' kidswear capsule in Apr 2026. Re-check for a Diwali 2026 drop before claiming the festive calendar is open. Reverie concentrated the moment in one store; Dehleez puts it at every door.
ips.cadence: Annual. Edition 01 is for Diwali 2027: the artist is announced in August 2027, portrait slots open three weeks before Diwali, and the run lasts from Navratri to Bhai Dooj. Thresholds install in two waves. For Diwali 2026 (8 Nov) we only record per-store festive footfall as the baseline.
ips.channels: The 311 thresholds; WhatsApp portrait booking and delivery; the film and family clips on @westside; Hindi, Marathi, Telugu, Kannada, Bengali and Assamese cuts; art and design press as well as fashion press; OOH near flagships.
ips.cast: One artist a year, drawn from FRONT ROW or a living craft tradition and named as large as Westside. WestStyleClub families across generations and regions. Store teams as portrait crew, trained by the house photographer. YNG photographers in the portrait stores.
art_direction: The threshold is the only decoration: one motif in three colours chosen by the artist, never the default festive red and gold. No fairy-light clutter, marigold strings or 'Diwali Sale' near any hero image.
Use real light only: one soft 2700K key and one real lit diya in each family's hands, with no fill flash.
Shoot formal, frontal portraits slightly from above, so the floor design reads, like an old studio photograph.
Cast grandparents to babies, from every region and of every build. Families style themselves from the capsule with store stylists.
Set 'DEHLEEZ EDITION 01' with दहलीज़ at equal size, the artist's name as large as Westside's, and the store dateline in uppercase sans. Each print carries only the family name and the store.
Commission one track, a reworked aarti or folk melody, for the film, the stores and every Reel.
ips.store_hook: BOOK a free 10-minute family portrait at your own store's Dehleez on WhatsApp, with a Studiowest touch-up first. Families arrive dressed, often styled in store from the capsule. They leave with a printed portrait and get the file on WhatsApp within 24 hours.
episode_examples: Dehleez Edition 01: <artist, announced Aug 2027> designs the door
Dehleez Portraits: four generations at Westside <store>, Pune
Dehleez, the film: 30 families, 30 thresholds, one diya
ips.hero_visual: A four-generation family stands barefoot on a marigold, kohl and ivory threshold at a Westside entrance, the grandmother holding a single lit diya. It is shot slightly from above, like a 1960s studio portrait, with 'DEHLEEZ EDITION 01 / दहलीज़' small in one corner.

ips.name: FIVE FUNCTIONS
ips.line: Bring your shaadi card to any Westside and a stylist plans your haldi, mehendi, sangeet, wedding and reception looks in one session. Five short wedding-video episodes follow real guests doing exactly that.
ips.role: The wedding-season driver, run without a discount, and the Mausam Shaadi issue (November to February). It turns the invitation in every Indian home into a reason to visit, and booked alterations build in a second visit. The Serial's film rules are kept; its scale is cut.
ips.precedent: Zara has premiered genre films on its own channels. 'Le Dîner' (11 Dec 2025) was a roughly 15-minute Christmas film premiered at 20:00 in the Zara app, then cut for social. Willy Chavarria's telenovela-style 'Vatisimo' followed on 26 Mar 2026. The two Kate Moss for Zara editions were each set by a real occasion: party season, then festival season.
ips.format:
Five 3-4 minute episodes in the language of an Indian wedding video. Each has one real guest and one function, and every guest is styled in a named store. They premiere one a night at 21:00 in WestStyleClub WhatsApp and the app, then are cut for Reels and Shorts. There is no long cut.

In store, 45-minute 'Bring the Card' sessions run, booked on WhatsApp or as walk-ins. Looks are held and alterations booked with a collection date.
ips.cadence: One numbered edition a year. Edition 01 pilots on the Jan-Feb 2027 wedding dates in one store, read with its city cluster, after alteration capacity is checked. From Edition 02 (Nov 2027) it is the nationwide Mausam Shaadi issue, with episodes released the week before the first peak dates. Bring the Card runs from November to February.
ips.channels: WestStyleClub WhatsApp and app premiere; @westside and YouTube; shareable links built for family WhatsApp groups; regional-language cuts; wedding planners and venues in the pilot city.
ips.cast: Real wedding guests from WestStyleClub (the cousin flying in, the groom's college friend, the mausi), paid and consenting. FRONT ROW New Faces in supporting roles. Store stylists and the store's alterations tailor as themselves.
art_direction: Play the genre straight. Each episode uses one wedding-video device (the slow-motion entrance, the family line-up, the varmala lift), shot with cinema restraint. No drones, lens flares or filters, and nothing that mocks the family.
Lock one colour to each function: haldi yellow, mehendi green, sangeet midnight, wedding red, reception ivory. Costume, set and title cards follow it.
Shoot at real venues at the real hour of the function, lit by the venue's own tungsten and string lights.
The trial room is the recurring set. Every episode opens on hands opening a real card, then cuts to the same Westside trial room.
Cast across communities and budgets: a Marwari sangeet, a Telugu haldi, a Bengali reception. Menswear (E.T.A., KALA by E.T.A.) gets equal screen time.
Put no price, logo bug or call to action inside the film. Title cards read 'EPISODE 03 · SANGEET' with a Devanagari subtitle, and each episode closes on the store dateline and full credits.
ips.store_hook: Show your wedding invitation, printed or on WhatsApp, at any Westside, or BOOK ahead with the code CARD. A stylist plans all five functions in one 45-minute session, holds the looks in a trial room and books alterations with a collection date, which brings you back.

ips.name: THE REGULARS
ips.line: Westside's creator ladder, built on WestStyleClub: your membership ID is your creator ID, your home store is your stage, and you move up on store bills and visits, not clicks.
ips.role: The volume and community engine. It folds the Style Collective, YNG's 4,000 creators, Wesness run captains and FRONT ROW's 150 culture-shapers into one ladder, with one ID and one monthly brief. It carries the system's humour (The Bench), the 72-hour Burst and the Westside run. Start Line is folded in as the Runner track.
ips.precedent: Zara's The Fold-er (12 Jun 2026) brings creators onto Zara's own surfaces under house art direction rather than renting their feeds. Zara Athleticz's 2026 named runner 'curator' drew criticism from the running community, so Wesness captains are credited as captains. Wesness runs already start at Westside stores (Gachibowli, New Commercial Street, Sky Vista D.N. Nagar). Target's creator programmes (Club Target / Target Ambassadors with LTK, Target Circle) appear only in our brief and model memory, with no verified source; none of them goes in the deck until verified.
ips.format:
Four tiers named after the store (FLOOR, RAIL, WINDOW, FRONT ROW) on four tracks (Stylist, Creator, Runner, Culture). Each month brings one central brief with templates, three permitted shot grammars (mirror, pavement, trial room) and a fixed 1.5-second end card: 'Seen at Westside, <store>, <city>'.

The Bench is a monthly 'bas dekh rahe hain' creator brief, plus a bench outside the trial rooms in pilot stores.

The Runner track is a monthly Wesness store-start or store-finish run in each city, in 2-5K women's formats, on a numbered route card. There is also one at each full-tier First Look.
ips.cadence: Always on. Monthly brief and a Regulars Night in each pilot store, with tiers reviewed quarterly. The pilot runs in one city cluster (about 300 creators and 30-50 stylists). After that, 3-5 Regulars per store, with a new cohort recruited at every opening.
ips.channels: Creators' own Instagram and YouTube, tagged to a named store (never just 'Westside'); WestStyleClub WhatsApp for briefs, codes and attribution; bylined pieces in the app's Trial Room section; Wesness WhatsApp communities.
ips.cast: WestStyleClub members, YNG/NIFT creators and designers, Style Collective stylists, Wesness run captains, FRONT ROW culture-shapers and store associates.
art_direction: Creators keep their own face, voice and language, inside three shot grammars and one monthly hero edit.
Natural light only: no ring lights and no face filters.
The location tag is always a named store.
Use a fixed end card: white uppercase sans on black reading 'Seen at Westside, <store>, <city>', with the tier badge.
Put ASCI disclosure (#ad or #collab) in the first line of every caption template.
Humour lives here, not in brand production. The Indian shopping ritual is the joke, never the customer or the product. Hinglish as people speak it, subtitled.
ips.store_hook: Every perk is redeemed in a store: kit pickup, Thursday-night Window previews, trial-room shoot slots, priority bookings and Regulars Night. Each creator's home-store code is captured at the billing counter against their WestStyleClub ID. Runners check in at the store door with the route-card QR. Runs are held only at high-street stores with legal early access, or timed to finish at opening, with chai and the activewear rail.

art_direction_bible: ONE HOUSE CREW. Umashan Naidoo is house creative director. One external photographer, one stylist and one art director are contracted for at least four Mausam issues, and they shoot the reference images for every property. There are no per-label photographers. Store VM leads, stylists and staff are credited by name.
PORTRAIT FIRST. Each frame holds one figure, or one family, full-length or three-quarter, with headroom. Never cut at the hem. No product grids, flat-lays or catalogue smiles on any hero image.

INDIA AS ARCHITECTURE. Shoot one real place per issue or episode, as it is: a Chandigarh corridor, a Mumbai stairwell, a Pune lawn. The store itself counts as a place: its window, curtain, threshold and the pavement outside. No added props and no studio fakes of Indian streets.

ONE LIGHT. Use daylight from one direction and keep the shadows. Indoors, use one warm key at 2700-3200K. No ring lights, gels, LED chasers, fill flash or beauty filters. Monsoon is shot in real rain.

THREE NAMED COLOURS. Each Mausam issue declares three colours by name on its cover. They carry through to the window planes, the trial-room wall, signage, the WhatsApp header and the film grade. Never default to festive red and gold; the Dehleez colours are chosen by the artist.
NO RETAIL NOISE ON A HERO. No price, offer, '% off', 'NEW', 'SALE', hashtag or call to action appears on any hero image or inside any film. Commerce lives on the rail card, the app page and WhatsApp.

NUMBER AND DATELINE. Every asset carries its number and the dateline 'SEEN AT WESTSIDE, <STORE>, <CITY>' in small uppercase sans at bottom left, with the numerals in the serif. The address is the brand.

WESTSIDE'S OWN MARK, PLUS A SCRIPT ZARA CANNOT OWN. The existing Westside wordmark is the masthead and is never redrawn or reset. A hairline Devanagari or regional-script second mark signs every property: मौसम, दहलीज़, or the city in its own script.

CAST INDIA AS IT IS. Cast real members and neighbours across regions, ages, sizes and skin tones. Every set includes someone over 55, and a child where it is a family moment. Studiowest make-up stays natural. No skin lightening, slimming or heavy retouching. Everyone is paid and signs a release; minors need guardian consent.

ONE ANGLE PER PROPERTY, so that every archive reads as one grid:
- The Window: straight on at eye height, from the same reference store each week.
- Seen In: one focal length and one camera height.
- The Trial Room: through the curtain, from a fixed rig at chest height.
- First Look: portraits at one distance.

INDIAN GENRES, PLAYED STRAIGHT. Films borrow an Indian form, such as the wedding video, the studio portrait or the silent monsoon film. They use locked-off frames and long takes, never parody. Only two films a year, each with full credits at the end and no logo bug.

CLEAN GLASS. Each window bay carries one programme per week, set by the glass calendar. No festoons, balloon arches, ribbon, vinyl or 'Grand Opening'. At an opening, one local maker's object stands alone in the window. At Diwali, the threshold is the only decoration.

AUTHORED SOUND AND LANGUAGE. Commission one track per Mausam issue and reuse it in the film, in store and as the Reels sound; everywhere else, use room tone. Hinglish and regional languages are used as people speak them, with subtitles.

EXPENSIVE BY RESTRAINT, NOT SPEND. Use fixed rigs, store teams trained as portrait crew, one reference store for The Window, and phone capture to the house spec. The money goes on the crew and the edit, never on props.
naming_and_voice: Property names are plain English nouns from the store or from Indian life (The Window, The Trial Room, Seen In, First Look, Five Functions, The Regulars). The alternative is one Hindi-Urdu word the whole country knows (Mausam, Dehleez), which is always shown with its Devanagari form (मौसम, दहलीज़). No portmanteaus, puns or hashtags as names.
Use one dateline: 'SEEN AT WESTSIDE, <STORE>, <CITY>', with the store name exactly as it appears on Trent's store list. Never write 'Westside' alone where a store can be named.
There are only three store verbs: BOOK (a stylist, a room, a portrait), HOLD (a size) and RSVP (a guest list). The WhatsApp keyword is the verb plus the property code: 'HOLD 047', 'BOOK 012', 'CARD'.
Interface copy is Zara-terse: uppercase nouns and imperatives. No exclamation marks, emoji, superlatives, 'hurry' or 'limited time'. State numbers plainly ('311 STORES').

Descriptions start with the thing, in short factual sentences: 'A weekly look, every Friday, in every window.' Label names appear in small capitals exactly as on the tag: E.T.A., KALA by E.T.A., Utsa, Vark, Bombay Paisley, Wardrobe, LOV, Nuon, Studiowest.
Titles use the subject's own words ('My brother's sangeet, and no lehenga'). Credits name people by first name, age and neighbourhood (Seen In), or by name and role (staff).

The voice is warm and specific: a well-dressed friend at the store, not a luxury house and not a sale flyer. Humour lives in The Regulars' briefs, not in brand production. The Indian shopping ritual is the joke, never the customer, the family or the product.
Speak India's languages as they are spoken. Use Hinglish where people use it, with English subtitles. Dehleez and Five Functions get Hindi, Marathi, Telugu, Kannada, Bengali and Assamese cuts.
Owned phrases are earned, not invented. 'Every look has an address' is ours. 'Bas dekh rahe hain' and 'the Westside run' are seeded through Regulars briefs and kept only if members pick them up.

Never say 'luxury', 'affordable luxury', 'Zara at Westside prices', 'Grand Opening', 'Sale', 'dhamaka' or 'mega'. Competitors are never named in consumer copy. Zara is named only in the pitch, on its reference screen.
Every creator post carries ASCI disclosure (#ad or #collab) in its first line and a named-store location tag.

deck_storyboard.headline: SEEN AT WESTSIDE
deck_storyboard.support: Every look has an address. A content-IP system from Mask360, October 2026.
details: A proposal to Westside (Trent Ltd) from Mask360.
Eight properties, one house look and one measure: footfall per store.
It starts with one store for eight weeks.

deck_storyboard.headline: Built like Zara. Counted at the till.
deck_storyboard.support: Content IP made the way the best fashion brands make it, moving people from the post to the billing counter.
details: Westside's ambition: beat Zara in India.
The brief: content IP built like Zara and Target Style build it, beautifully.
Mask360's promise: from the post to the billing counter, measured on footfall per store.
Start with one store: a launch or a festive drop.
deck_storyboard.visual: A white screen with black text only. The brief is set as three uppercase lines, and the word STORE has a 1px hairline underline. No image.

deck_storyboard.headline: 311 stores. 94% in store.
deck_storyboard.support: Oct 2025 to Oct 2026: a store business run on a member database, growing by opening doors.
details: Stores: 278 (Dec 2025) to 311 (30 Sep 2026). Openings are lumpy: 23 in Q4 FY26, 1 net in Q1 FY27, 10 net in Q2 FY27.
About 94% of sales are in store. Online is about 6%, despite 25-38% growth.
11.85M active WestStyleClub members carry over 90% of revenue (FY26 MD&A).
Fashion like-for-like growth has been low single digits or negative for five quarters. Growth comes from new stores.
Marketing ran through owned IP: Wesness (3,500+ women at the Mumbai run, 8 Feb 2026), YNG (4,000 creators, 6M views), the W.i.S.H. capsule and FRONT ROW (1 Oct 2026).
deck_storyboard.visual: A Zara-style listing grid of six 3:4 tiles. Each holds a single serif numeral on white (311 / 94% / 11.85M / 25,000 / 4,000 / 400-500) with an uppercase label as the 'price line'. Tapping a tile opens its source in the info panel.

deck_storyboard.headline: Bigger than Zara. Not yet busier.
deck_storyboard.support: Westside has 311 stores to Zara India's 22, but each Zara store sells several times more, and Westside's content rarely names a store.
details: Scale: 311 stores against 22. Westside's derived revenue is about ₹5,000 cr against Zara India's ₹2,749 cr (an estimate; Westside revenue is not disclosed).
Productivity: a Zara store sells roughly 3-7 times what a Westside store sells (a rough calculation).
We found no Diwali or wedding-season film, and about 40 openings in Q3-Q4 FY26 got almost no launch coverage.
The owned platforms report views and turnout, not store visits.
Westside makes 400-500 designs a week, but there is no day people know to come in.
deck_storyboard.visual: A split screen. On the left, '311' in huge serif with '22' small beneath it. On the right, a 3x3 grid of generic catalogue frames, each with an empty location tag reading '—'. No competitor imagery.

deck_storyboard.headline: Every look has an address.
deck_storyboard.support: Seen at Westside: one magazine with 311 addresses.
details: Every asset carries a number and a dateline: 'WINDOW No. 047 · SEEN AT WESTSIDE, <STORE>, <CITY>'.

The WestStyleClub ID captured at the counter links post, booking, visit and bill.
One brand handle (@westside), the app and WestStyleClub WhatsApp. Creators post on their own handles, tagged to a store.
It is Westside's own Indian calendar, made with Zara's restraint. It is not 'Zara at Westside prices'.
