UI grammar inspired by fashion retail apps; not affiliated with Zara/Inditex or Target.
deck_storyboard.visual: A black screen with Westside's wordmark centred in white and the dateline 'SEEN AT WESTSIDE, <YOUR STORE>' beneath it, then MASK360 small. Behind a 30% scrim, a 6-second loop of Window No. 001 being dressed at night.

ui_rules: ONE SCREEN = ONE VIEWPORT. Each screen is 100svh. The deck container uses scroll-snap-type: y mandatory with scroll-snap-stop: always. Navigation: swipe on phone; ArrowUp/ArrowDown, PageUp/PageDown and Space on desktop. The URL hash (#12) tracks the screen, so a link lands on a slide.

CHAPTER TABS like the Zara app's section row. Along the top runs a row of uppercase tabs: THE BRIEF / THE IDEA / THE IPs / THE STORE / THE PILOT / SCALE / MASK360. The active tab gets a 1px underline. Tapping a tab jumps to that chapter, and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight move between chapters.

MASTHEAD SCALE. The wordmark is huge (40-60% of viewport width on phone) only on the cover and chapter openers; everywhere else it is 18-22px tall. Never reset the Westside wordmark in a font, and never draw, trace or approximate the ZARA logo.
MINIMAL ON-SCREEN TEXT. Each screen shows only a 10-11px uppercase section label, one headline of at most 8 words, and one support line of at most 20 words. Everything else lives in the info panel.

EXPANDABLE INFO PANEL. An uppercase 'DETAILS +' label opens it.
- Phone: a white bottom sheet with square corners and a 1px top hairline. It slides up in 250ms to at most 70% height, and closes with a swipe down or ESC.
- Desktop: a right-hand column.
- Contents: 2-5 bullets, then sources in 10px grey.
- Property screens add native <details> accordions: FORMAT & CADENCE, IN STORE, MEASUREMENT, PRECEDENT & SOURCES.
PROPERTY SCREENS ARE PRODUCT PAGES. A full-bleed hero (stacked images on desktop), then the name, cadence and KPI line, then a black, square-cornered ADD TO PILOT button that increments PILOT [n].

THE SYSTEM SCREEN IS A LISTING PAGE. Use 3:4 cards with 0-2px gutters and an uppercase name under each. Cadence and KPI take the place of the price line. Include a working 1/2/4-column density switch.

TYPE.
- Inter Tight for all UI and text, weights 300/400/500 only; bold reads as Target, not Zara.
- UI labels: uppercase, 11-13px, tracking +0.03 to +0.06em.
- Body: sentence case, 13-15px, line-height 1.45, max 36ch.
- Headlines: uppercase Inter Tight 300 at 28-40px on phone and 56-88px on desktop.
- Numerals: Bodoni Moda.
- Tabular figures on every KPI line.

COLOUR.
- UI screens: #000 on #FFF.
- Photographs: #FFF type, with a 20-30% black scrim only behind the text.
- Secondary grey #767676; hairlines rgba(0,0,0,.12).
- The only accent is the current Mausam colour, used in chips and the calendar, never as decoration.
- No gradients, shadows, rounded corners or pills.
- Dark mode inverts the chrome only, never the photographs.

IMAGES. Full-bleed with object-fit: cover. Supply art-directed <picture> crops for 9:16 (phone) and 16:9 (desktop) so faces and hems are never cut. No borders or frames. Every hero carries a 10-11px uppercase grey credit line (PHOTOGRAPHY / STYLING / LOCATION: WESTSIDE <STORE>), and every comp or generated image is marked MOCK-UP.

MOTION. Use plain cuts and fades of 200-300ms ease-out, with no bounce or playful micro-animation. Video plays autoplay muted loop playsinline, with a poster frame and a small uppercase SOUND ON toggle. prefers-reduced-motion disables autoplay and animated snapping.
MICROCOPY. Use uppercase nouns and imperatives: VIEW, DETAILS, ADD TO PILOT, BOOK, HOLD, RSVP. No exclamation marks, emoji or superlatives. State numbers plainly ('311 STORES').

HAMBURGER INDEX. A full-height left panel: the chapter tabs on top, then every screen's headline as an uppercase list. Tapping a title jumps to that screen, so the index doubles as the table of contents in the meeting.

PHONE-FIRST. Design at 390x844 and test at 360px with a 16px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll. Desktop keeps the same full-bleed screens at 16:9, with the info panel on the right. Tap targets are at least 44px, focus rings are visible, and every image has alt text.

DATA SCREENS LOOK LIKE ZARA UTILITY PAGES, NOT CHARTS. Use order-summary rows with hairline dividers and tabular numerals. Mark any illustrative number as such; empty result cells show '—', never invented figures.

REFERENCE HYGIENE. No Zara or Target logos, product photos or screenshots anywhere. The reference screen is text-only, with dates and source links. The last screen and the speaker notes carry the line: 'UI grammar inspired by fashion retail apps; not affiliated with Zara/Inditex or Target.'

DELIVERY. Ship one self-contained HTML file that works offline. Self-host the fonts as woff2 with font-display: swap and include their OFL licences. Compress images (AVIF/WebP with JPEG fallback) so the file stays small enough to email.
final.font_recommendation:
UI font: Inter Tight (Google Fonts, SIL OFL 1.1, free), weights 300, 400 and 500.
- Why: Zara's UI reads as a light, small, uppercase grotesque in the Helvetica family (the exact cut is unverified). Neue Helvetica needs a paid web licence. The free Helvetica clones (TeX Gyre Heros, Nimbus Sans, FreeSans) have no Light weight, so they cannot reproduce that lightness.
- Inter Tight ships weights 100-900, Light included. Its tight default spacing suits uppercase labels and headlines, it is drawn for screens, and Inter's tabular figures keep the KPI lines aligned.

Logo: Westside's existing wordmark, used as supplied vector artwork and never reset in a typeface. Resetting it in a Didone would read as a pastiche of Zara's masthead.

Display font: Bodoni Moda (Google Fonts, SIL OFL 1.1, free; weights 400-900 with an optical-size axis).
- Use it only for numerals and the rare single display word ('No. 047', '311', 'Edition 01').
- Set it at opsz 96, weight 400-500, tracking about -0.04em.
- Why: its high-contrast Didone strokes give the fashion-magazine signal at large sizes without touching the masthead.

Script companion: neither face covers Indic scripts. For the Devanagari second marks (मौसम, दहलीज़) add Noto Serif Devanagari (OFL) at weight 200-300, and use the matching Noto faces for regional city cuts.

Setup: self-host all of them as woff2. Fallback stack: 'Inter Tight', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif. The current build in pitches/westside loads Hanken Grotesk from Google Fonts; switch it to self-hosted Inter Tight so the deck uses one UI face and works offline.
risks_and_checks: TARGET CLAIMS. Remove every Target claim from the deck: Club Target/LTK and its 6 May 2026 date, the @TargetStyle formats, 'Target run', Target Circle, Order Pickup, Wonderland and the 2019 anniversary collection. None of them has a dated URL. Present the principles as Mask360's own until each one is verified.

ZARA OVERSTATEMENTS TO FIX OR KEEP OUT.
- Studio's crew is documented only for recent seasons, not 'since 2016'.
- SRPLS is twice-yearly and its numbering starts at CLLCTN 02 (Spring 2019), not Nov 2018. That the run is 'collectible' is our inference.
- Zara premieres collections, not store openings.
- 50 Years, 50 Icons did not tie its faces to the first store, and cutting one clip per face is something it could do, not a documented practice.
- SS25 'On the Road' was cast with models, not street-cast.
- We cannot claim the 'teleshopping' critique caused Streaming to be scaled back.
- Try-On markets: 43 in the results release, 26 in the annual report.
- Store Mode's fitting-room booking is documented only in 2020-23 coverage.
- The window refresh cycle and the Hong Kong LED façade rest on weak sources.
- 'No price on a hero image' is our reading of coverage, not an audit.
- The Athleticz curator drew a backlash.
- The 2025 Spanish 10K record is sourced to an article that predates it.

ZARA INDIA FESTIVE CHECK. We found no sequel to Reverie (15 Oct 2024), but that is a negative search, and Zara India ran 'Curated At Home' kidswear in Apr 2026. Navratri began on 11 Oct 2026 and Diwali is 8 Nov 2026. Search for a Zara India Diwali 2026 drop the day before sending, and phrase any claim as 'none found as of <date>'.

WESTSIDE FACTS.
- 11.85M is the WestStyleClub active membership (FY26 MD&A), not the WhatsApp channel. Other Trent material gives 19M+ or 16.4M, so confirm the definition.
- Guwahati and Gachibowli are existing stores, not new ones.
- FY26 net additions are reported as 52 or 60; Q4 FY26 had 22-23, Q1 FY27 1 net and Q2 FY27 10 net.
- AGM guidance was about 50 stores a year. Bloomberg's 100 a year was later described by Trent as not guidance, so word '50-100 planned' carefully.

STORE NUMBERING. Confirm with Trent how store numbers are assigned through closures, relocations and consolidations before 'First Look No. 312' goes on a slide. Cite Trent's own 243rd-store release as the precedent for numbering.

WEEKLY NEWNESS. 400-500 designs a week (Bloomberg / Retail Insight Network, Jul 2026) anchors The Window's cadence. Confirm with Westside that one own label can supply a windowable look family every week, in sizes for 311 stores and in kits that fit small mall bays.

ILLUSTRATIVE STORE NAMES. Kalyani Nagar, Banjara Hills, Koramangala, Salt Lake, Sky Vista D.N. Nagar, Bandra and the Hyderabad 'No. 312' are illustrative. Lock each one to Trent's store list or replace it with <STORE>.
RE-EDITION STAYS PARKED. Confirm that archive prints, patterns and deadstock exist, and verify the founding year (reportedly 1998), before mentioning it anywhere.

WESNESS. Confirm the current rhythm: roughly monthly paid runs of 2-5K at ₹399-699, with nothing found after Jul 2026. Confirm which stores have legal early access and what the mall rules allow. Year one has no 05:45 openings, no certified 10K and no 'curator' title.

MEASUREMENT.
- Confirm whether stores have people counters. If not, install them before a Q4 FY27 opening, using the same hardware in test and control stores and calibrating with a manual count.
- Agree the control stores, the minimum detectable lift (about 10%) and the definition of 'inconclusive' before launch.
- Keep Westside's national activity identical in test and control stores.
- Match the January end-of-season sale in the controls.

PRIVACY AND CONSENT.
- Use aggregate counters that store no identities.
- Full compliance with the DPDP Rules is due by 13 May 2027, so WestStyleClub consent must cover measurement and any offline-conversion use with Meta or Google.
- Get signed releases, pay fees, and get guardian consent for everyone filmed.
- Make no 'Style Call Log' from real calls.
- Build ASCI disclosure into every creator template.

POSITIONING AND GROUP SENSITIVITY. Never use 'Zara at Westside prices'. Trent still holds about 20% of Zara India, so clear the Zara references with the Westside contact. Use no Zara imagery or logos, and keep the 'not affiliated' line.

GAP-SCREEN NUMBERS. Westside's derived revenue (about ₹5,000 cr) and 'Zara sells 3-7x per store' are rough derivations, because Westside revenue is not disclosed. Label them as estimates or drop them.
CALENDAR. Check the 2027 dates for Navratri, Diwali, Bhai Dooj, Durga Puja, Ganesh Chaturthi and Bihu, and the peak wedding dates for Jan-Feb 2027 in the pilot city.

NAMES. Run trademark and meaning checks in classes 25 and 35 on Seen at Westside, Mausam, Dehleez, Five Functions, Seen In, First Look and The Regulars. For Dehleez, confirm the transliteration and the Devanagari दहलीज़ with Hindi and Urdu reviewers. Check the regional-language cuts with native speakers.
VISUALS. Every hero image is a mock-up and must be labelled as one. Do not use real customers' likenesses without consent, and do not let AI-generated people pass as real members.

COMMERCIALS AND AGENCY CONTEXT. This system carries no budget or fee. The existing build proposes a fee contingent on footfall; confirm the terms and cost the production cap before sending. Westside's creative has been in-house under Umashan Naidoo, and Oktobuzz has been named as its social agency. Position Mask360 as the bridge to the store that works with both, and confirm the contact's role.

FONTS AND FILE. Check that the shipped subset of Inter Tight includes tabular figures and the ₹ glyph. Use Bodoni Moda for numerals only. Self-host the fonts and ship the OFL licences. Test the HTML at 360px and offline. The current build uses Hanken Grotesk and fonts hosted by Google.

scores.lens: Zara lens: SEEN AT WESTSIDE / 'The magazine you walk into' (Mausam, The Window, The Trial Room, Store No., Roshni, The Serial, Re-Edition)
strengths: Has the strongest art-direction system of the three slates, and the only one that would hold up next to Zara Studio content. Each issue shoots one real Indian location as architecture, in daylight from one direction. It declares three colours per issue, uses a hairline Devanagari मौसम as a second mark, and puts no price on any image.

MAUSAM is the best single idea in any slate. It numbers issues by India's real seasons (Garmi, Baarish, Tyohaar, Shaadi), and Zara's SS/FW calendar cannot claim those. The three declared colours carry through to windows, signage and the film grade.
It merges the draft IPs with discipline. The Trial Room absorbs the Style Collective bylines and the Style Call booking. The 72-hour Burst and Style Call become mechanics rather than properties.
Store No. has a clever built-in return trip: the first-30 portraits are printed and handed over a week later. Numbering by store count matches Trent's own habit ('243rd store' press releases).
Cheap local footfall levers: The Window updates every store's Google Business Profile photo the same morning, and reserve-to-try holds a size until Sunday close.
Its caveats are the most honest: no Target precedent is cited, and Roshni is pushed to Diwali 2027.
weaknesses: Production load is the heaviest of the three slates and unrealistic for Westside's budget. Each year it needs four location shoots and four films, 52 centrally prototyped windows, a six-episode cinema-crew serial plus a 40-minute cut, a 3-4 m sculpture plus a light object in all 311 windows, two designer volumes, and 3-day premieres with a 4-person travelling crew at every opening. Openings are lumpy (23 in Q4 FY26, 1 net in Q1 FY27), so one crew cannot cover a quarter's wave.

The windows collide. The Mausam cover goes into all 311 windows, The Window bay changes every Friday, Roshni puts a light object in every bay, and Store No. puts an artist object in the window. No glass calendar says which one wins in which week.

Creator scale and owned language are weak. Creators are demoted to a 'mechanic', there is no humour and no consumer phrase, and the tone risks reading cold to Westside's value-conscious family shopper.

The big moments concentrate footfall in one store. Roshni's sculpture stands in one flagship and Re-Edition sells in one new store for three days, so 300+ stores get a scaled object or nothing. With LFL at low single digits, the mature estate needs the help most.
Mausam's KPI (issue week against the prior four weeks) is confounded by seasonality. A national cover in all 311 stores in the same week leaves no control group.
It positions Westside as 'Zara at Westside prices', which invites a comparison Westside loses. Trent still holds about 20% of Zara India, so the framing could also be awkward inside the group.
It overstates precedents: 'the same team every SS and FW since 2016', 'Zara premieres each big drop in one room', 'did not return' to Diwali.

scores.lens: Target lens: Seen at Westside / 'Every look has an address' (two surfaces: @westside plus a new @seenatwestside channel; The Window, The Trial Room, Seen In, The Regulars, Editions, Just Looking, The Function, First Look)
strengths: It is the only slate with ownable consumer language and humour: 'bas dekh rahe hain', The Bench, 'the Westside run'. It sells the trip, not the product, which suits a business with about 94% of sales in store.

Seen In is the best low-cost property in any slate. A pavement seamless goes up outside a named store, the neighbourhood is cast in its own clothes, the prints hang in that store the next week, and subjects collect them, which brings the family back. It also feeds casting for every other property.

The Regulars uses the right attribution model: membership ID as creator ID, home store as stage, and tier progress on member-attributed bills and visits rather than clicks. It folds in Style Collective, YNG, Wesness captains and FRONT ROW.
A fixed weekly rhythm teaches people when to look. City specials (Durga Puja in Kolkata, Ganesh Chaturthi in Pune, Bihu in Guwahati) give real regional India fit.
It labels every Target precedent UNVERIFIED and moves The Function's Season 1 to the Jan-Feb 2027 wedding dates.
weaknesses: It launches a second handle (@seenatwestside) from zero followers. That splits reach and goes against the research lesson to split accounts only when the grammar differs.

It contradicts itself. The house rule says one fixed photographer, but Editions has one photographer per label (about 9). The architecture puts Seen In on Sunday, but the property says 'published Monday', which is Just Looking's slot. The Function Ep. 1 is a Diwali card party inside a Jan-Feb season.
Editions (a monthly label film, a commissioned track and a per-label photographer) is the costliest and least store-measurable item in the slate, and it breaks up the house look.
Just Looking's KPI is shares and forwards, not footfall. Brand-produced comedy sketches can slide into sitcom-TVC territory that a Zara creative director would reject.
Beauty is uneven. Comedy, soap triple zooms and nine label identities pull against one magazine look.
Feasibility claims are inflated: 30-50 stylists 'scaling to about 1,500', a well-known actor as the matriarch, nightly episodes, and watch parties in 10 flagships.

Its facts slip. The 11.85M WestStyleClub members are presented as WhatsApp channel members. It calls Guwahati 'Westside's first night in the north-east' and uses Gachibowli as a new-store pilot, but both cities already have Westside stores.
The whole lens rests on Target precedents that come from the brief or model memory. None can go in a deck.

scores.lens: Footfall lens: Seen at Westside / 'Every look has an address' (The Window, The Trial Room, Dateline, Style Call, Start Line, First Look, Dehleez, Five Functions)
strengths: Every asset ends in BOOK, HOLD or RSVP through that store's WhatsApp with a property code, and the WestStyleClub ID is captured at the counter. That gives true post-to-bill attribution per store.

Its measurement design is the best of the three: a staggered Window rollout that creates its own control stores, matched control stores, mall footfall counters, and like-for-like year-on-year reads for festive and wedding.

DEHLEEZ is the best festive idea in any slate. One artist designs the threshold of all 311 doors, a ritual space in Indian homes, and families book a dressed-up portrait standing on it. The festive footfall spreads across the whole network instead of one flagship.

Five Functions' 'Bring the Card' turns the wedding invitation in every Indian home into a ticket into the store. It sells five functions in one basket without a discount, and booking alterations for collection builds in a second visit.
The Window rail inside the door for seven days fixes the 'I saw it but can't find it' failure.
Wesness, YNG and FRONT ROW are plugged in with clear jobs, and the Style Collective becomes one cast pool by catchment.
weaknesses: Three overlapping stylist properties (Trial Room, Dateline, Style Call) serve one conversion path. They should be one property and one mechanic.

Style Call seven days a week at 300+ stores, with per-store numbers and pre-pulled looks, is a staffing and inventory programme, not content. The 'Style Call Log' edited from real customer calls raises consent and privacy risk.

Start Line misreads Wesness. Today Wesness runs roughly monthly paid 2-5K women's runs, and the slate jumps to weekly 5K/10K at 06:00 from a different store each week. Mall stores cannot open at 05:45. A certified 10K adds permits and cost, and naming a 'curator' repeats the Athleticz move that drew a running-community backlash.
It has the least ownable language of the three and no humour, so Target-style scale is weak.
Beauty is uneven: the WhatsApp cards and split-screen Log are utilitarian. Resetting the Westside wordmark in Bodoni Moda is an unrequested rebrand and reads as a pastiche of Zara's Didone masthead.
Dehleez's operations are not addressed: floor graphics at 311 entrances need slip-safety and mall approval, and 50+ staffed portrait studios have to run in peak trading week.

precedent_errors: Zara slate, MAUSAM: 'The same Meisel, Baron & Baron, Templer, McGrath and Palau team has shot every SS and FW since 2016' is unsupported. The research only says Studio launched as a fall 2016 capsule. Meisel's Studio work is documented from FW18-19, and the season-by-season record runs SS22-SS26. Continuity of the full team since 2016 is not evidenced. 'No image carries a price' is also the research's own inference, not an audit.

All three slates, THE WINDOW: SRPLS is a twice-yearly collection (CLLCTN 02 in Spring 2019 to CLLCTN 16 in Apr 2026), and Zara renews windows per campaign (an 18-20-day cycle comes from one weak source). There is no Zara precedent for a weekly numbered window. The weekly cadence should rest on Westside's own weekly newness (its AI design suite produces 400-500 designs a week), not on Zara.

Zara slate, THE WINDOW: 'numbered releases from Nov 2018' is wrong. The Nov 2018 launch was not numbered; numbering starts at CLLCTN 02 (Spring 2019). In all three slates, 'the run became collectible' is the research's own inference. The research records no sales or collector data and says 'longevity is the visible signal'.

Zara slate, THE WINDOW: the idea that windows are photographed centrally and copied by local teams rests on one weak secondary source (peru-retail). Only the A Coruña mock-up stores are supported (Business Insider 2018). The Hong Kong LED façade comes from an undated vendor case study.

Zara slate, STORE No.: 'Zara premieres each big drop in one room' is overgeneralised; SRPLS, Studio and the Kate Moss capsules show no such room. None of the cited examples (50 Creators, Galliano, Bad Bunny) is a store opening, so there is no Zara precedent for openings run as premieres. '50 Years, 50 Icons tied many faces to the first store' is also wrong: the film was released on the first store's anniversary and the store was redesigned, but the film did not feature or tie the faces to it.

Zara slate ROSHNI, Target slate THE FUNCTION, Footfall slate DEHLEEZ: 'Zara entered once and did not return' and 'left open since Reverie' rest on a negative search finding that the research says is not proof. Diwali 2026 is about three weeks away, and Reverie launched on 15 Oct 2024, so a 2026 Zara India festive drop could still appear. Zara India also ran a local 'Curated At Home' kidswear capsule in Apr 2026. Re-check before claiming the festive calendar is open.

Target slate, SEEN IN: Zara Studio SS25 'On the Road' was 'rough black-and-white studio portraits' with fresh-face model casting, referencing Avedon. The research does not support 'real people shot on a portable seamless on location'; that describes Avedon's own method. The precedent supports the look only, not street casting.

Target slate EDITIONS and Footfall slate DATELINE: 'Zara Man's named strands, each with one fixed photographer' misreads the research. The same photographer (Alvaro Perena Jimenez) shot Archive, Evening Edition, Sunglasses and FW26. The precedent supports one house photographer across strands, which contradicts Editions' 'one photographer per label'.

Target and Footfall slates: '50 Years, 50 Icons: one idea cut into one clip per face' is presented as documented Zara practice. The research gives it only as a capability ('it cuts down into dozens of single-face clips') and found no view figures.

Footfall slate, STYLE CALL: 'Zara Streaming ... scaled back after critics called it teleshopping' is a causal claim the research does not support. Per FashionUnited ES, the format was scaled back after episode 1, while the 'teletienda' critique was about episode 2 (28 Mar 2025). The figure of '43 markets' for Try-On also conflicts with the 26 in Inditex's annual report.

Footfall slate, START LINE: the Athleticz 'named running curator' is cited as a positive model, but the research records a backlash from the running community (Substack, Marathon Handbook). The 2025 Spanish women's 10K record (30:59) is sourced to a Sep 2024 article that predates it.
Target and Footfall slates, THE TRIAL ROOM: Store Mode's fitting-room booking with a 5-minute claim comes from 2020-23 coverage. Its current availability, including in India, is unverified.

Target slate, unverified throughout: Club Target / Target Ambassadors powered by LTK (6 May 2026), @TargetStyle's trend-edit, stylist-tip and street-style formats, 'Target run' adoption, owned-label personalities, Target Circle and Wonderland 2016 all come from the brief or model memory, with no URL. They are correctly flagged, but they cannot appear in the deck, and the lens's core logic currently rests on them. The Zara slate's Target 2019 anniversary archive (Re-Edition) is in the same position.

Zara slate architecture: 'mirrors Zara's quiet brand account and loud creator layer'. The quiet-account conventions come from weak single sources (NewswireJet, Sked Social), and the creator volumes are vendor estimates (Scrumball, Modash).

Non-precedent factual errors to fix. Target slate: '11.85M' is WestStyleClub's active membership, not the WhatsApp channel's. 'First Look No. 014: Guwahati, Westside's First Night in the North-East' is wrong, because Westside already has several Guwahati stores. Gachibowli, used as the new-store pilot, is an existing store and the Wesness start point. Target slate: 'about 1-2 openings a week' ignores the actual lumpiness (52 net in FY26, 1 net in Q1 FY27, 10 net in Q2 FY27). Footfall slate: Start Line assumes weekly 5K/10K Wesness runs, but Wesness currently runs roughly monthly paid 2-5K women's formats.

best_properties.name: THE WINDOW
best_properties.from_lens: Footfall (merged with the Zara and Target versions)
best_properties.why: It gives Westside a weekly newness signal on the most-seen surface it owns. The same numbered image goes up on the grid, the app, the WhatsApp header, the Google Business Profile and 311 windows. The Window rail inside the door and a WhatsApp HOLD make the look findable, and a staggered install gives a clean per-store control.
best_properties.fix: One bay and one look per store, with one own label a week in rotation (Zara slate). Anchor the weekly cadence to Westside's own weekly newness, not to SRPLS. Install nationally in two waves a week apart so every Window is also a test. In a Mausam launch week, that week's Window is the issue cover; no separate cover install. Keep the Thursday-night member preview, update the Google Business Profile photo the same morning, and rotate the hero store across cities. Ship a VM kit that works in small mall bays.

best_properties.name: THE TRIAL ROOM
best_properties.from_lens: Zara (with the Footfall Trial Room, Dateline and Style Call folded in)
best_properties.why: It is the one conversion path. The store's most private room becomes the set, bylined stylists become local names, and every episode and column ends with 'Book <stylist> at <store>', measured as booked visit, then bill, then ATV against walk-ins.
best_properties.fix: One weekly 45-60 second curtain episode (Footfall format), plus a fortnightly bylined column from 4 stylists in 4 pilot stores, using Dateline's city-dateline headline. Style Call (a 15-minute video call that converts to a held trial room) is the booking mechanic, not a separate property. Cap at 30-50 stylists in year one. Cast paid, consenting members. Set a booking-response SLA per store.

best_properties.name: FIRST LOOK (Store No.)
best_properties.from_lens: Zara and Footfall (Target's opening-day Seen In shoot folded in)
best_properties.why: It grows with the business: 50-100 planned openings, with growth now coming from new stores. Openings currently happen quietly. The property is numbered by store count (Trent already does this), with a guest list by pin code, one local maker's object in the window, a store-team masthead, and engineered return visits (first-30 portrait collection, 30-day Style Call card).
best_properties.fix: Two tiers. The full programme runs only for new cities, flagships and new formats. Infill stores get a kit: preview night, window object, entrance portraits and the 72-hour catchment burst. Drop the Day-2 livestream except in new cities. Plan crew capacity for clusters of 20+ openings in a quarter. Settle the numbering rule now, given consolidations. In the deck, say plainly that Zara premieres collections, not stores.

best_properties.name: SEEN IN
best_properties.why: It is the cheapest beautiful property in the set. A seamless goes up outside a named store, the neighbourhood is shot in its own clothes, the prints hang in that store, and subjects collect them, bringing family and joining WestStyleClub. It is also the casting engine for Mausam, First Look and the Regulars.
best_properties.fix: Shoot monthly per city, plus festival specials (Durga Puja, Ganesh Chaturthi, Bihu), instead of weekly. Run it on opening day at every full-tier First Look. Get signed releases and guardian consent for minors. Drop Zara SS25 as a street-casting precedent and present the format as Westside's own.

best_properties.name: DEHLEEZ
best_properties.from_lens: Footfall (absorbing ROSHNI's artist and light discipline)
best_properties.why: Every one of the 311 stores gets the festive moment at its own door. The threshold ritual is India-true, the booked family portrait brings a dressed-up multi-generation visit in peak season, and an annual numbered artist edition becomes a tradition Westside owns.
best_properties.fix: Take Roshni's rules: one artist named as large as Westside, three non-red/gold colours, real light as the only decoration, and a design-press push. Use a durable, anti-slip, mall-approved floor print rather than a 'rangoli sticker'. Run portrait studios in 50 stores in off-peak hours, staffed by trained store teams. Make Edition 01 Diwali 2027, with the artist announced in Aug 2027. It becomes the Mausam Tyohaar cover. Record Diwali 2026 per-store footfall now as the baseline.

best_properties.name: FIVE FUNCTIONS
best_properties.from_lens: Footfall (with the Zara Serial's and Target Function's film rules)
best_properties.why: 'Bring the Card' turns every wedding invitation into a reason to visit. It sells five functions in one basket without a discount, and alterations collection forces a second visit. Real-guest episodes are cheaper and more credible than a scripted soap.
best_properties.fix: Keep The Serial's rules: play the genre straight, use the trial room as a recurring set, one colour per function, and no logo bug or call to action in the film. Five 3-4 minute episodes with no 40-minute cut. Pilot the Jan-Feb 2027 wedding dates in one city cluster, with alteration capacity checked per store. It becomes the Mausam Shaadi issue.

best_properties.name: MAUSAM
best_properties.why: It is the ownable spine: India's real seasons as numbered issues, three declared colours across window, signage and grade, a Devanagari second mark, and one house crew. It gives the system the Zara-grade beauty the other slates lack, on ground Zara's SS/FW cannot take.
best_properties.fix: Make Mausam the frame, not a second production machine. Tyohaar is Dehleez and Shaadi is Five Functions, so only Garmi and Baarish are standalone shoots. Shoot stills and loops every issue, but only two films a year. Roll the cover out in two waves so issue weeks have controls, and read the KPI like-for-like year on year, not against the previous four weeks. Remove the 'same team since 2016' claim.

best_properties.name: THE REGULARS
best_properties.why: It is the volume engine, measured the way Westside makes money: membership ID as creator ID, home store as stage, in-store perks, and progression on member-attributed bills and sign-ups. One ladder replaces four separate communities.
best_properties.fix: Run it on @westside and creators' own handles; do not open a new @seenatwestside handle. Pilot in one city cluster (about 300 creators, 30-50 stylists). Capture creator codes at the counter against WestStyleClub IDs. Build ASCI disclosure into the templates. Fold Just Looking in as a monthly creator brief (The Bench). Do not cite Club Target until it is verified.

best_properties.name: RE-EDITION
best_properties.why: It draws newness from Westside's own archive in a quiet month. Scarcity comes from access, not price. Showing each original beside its rework, in black-and-white portraits, is beautiful and press-worthy.
best_properties.fix: Start once a year (Vol. 01 in Aug 2027), not twice. First confirm that archive prints, patterns and deadstock actually exist; Westside's founding year is also unverified. Premiere it by appointment in a high-traffic metro store, which need not be new, for three days, then 20 stores and the app. Keep prices inside the normal range. Drop Target 2019 as a precedent.

best_properties.name: START LINE
best_properties.why: Wesness already starts runs at Westside stores (Gachibowli, New Commercial Street, Sky Vista). A numbered route card and a QR check-in turn a 25,000-member community into WestStyleClub-linked store visits at almost no media cost.
best_properties.fix: Keep Wesness's real rhythm: a monthly store-start run per city, plus one at each full-tier First Look. Use only high-street stores with legal early access, or end the run at the store at opening time instead of opening at 05:45. Keep 2-5K women's formats. Use no 'curator' title, given the Athleticz backlash. Defer a certified 10K to year two at the earliest.

cut: ROSHNI as a standalone property. A single-flagship sculpture plus a light object in 311 windows is costly and concentrates footfall in one store. Fold the artist, three-colour and light-only rules into Dehleez.
THE SERIAL. Six 6-8 minute cinema-crew episodes, a 40-minute cut and weekly 'shop the episode' rails in every store are too heavy. Keep its film rules inside Five Functions.
THE FUNCTION. It duplicates the wedding moment, needs a well-known actor, and its Season 1 (Jan-Feb) includes a Diwali card-party episode.
EDITIONS. A monthly label film with a commissioned track and a photographer per label breaks the one-crew rule and is barely store-measurable. Label rotation lives inside The Window and Mausam.
JUST LOOKING as a weekly brand-produced comedy series. Keep the phrase, the Bench fixture in pilot stores, and a monthly Regulars creator brief.
DATELINE as a separate property. It merges into The Trial Room column.
STYLE CALL as a standalone property and the 'Style Call Log' film. Keep it as the booking mechanic, and drop the film because of consent and privacy risk.
The @seenatwestside handle and SEEN tab as a new channel. Use one handle, the app and WestStyleClub WhatsApp.
The 3-day premiere format (and Day-2 livestream) at every opening. Use a kit tier for infill stores.
Mausam films every quarter. Two films a year; stills and loops otherwise.
Weekly 06:00 Start Line from a different store, 05:45 store openings, and the certified Wesness 10K in year one.
Livestreams outside new-city First Looks. Zara itself scaled Streaming back.
A separate Mausam cover install in all 311 windows. The Window bay carries it in issue week.
Resetting the Westside wordmark in Bodoni Moda.
'Zara at Westside prices' as the positioning line, and any Target precedent without a verified URL.
Scaling targets of 1,500 stylists or 300 columnists. Year one is 30-50 stylists.
recommendations: Platform: 'Seen at Westside', with the line 'Every look has an address.' Every asset carries a number and the dateline 'SEEN AT WESTSIDE, <STORE>, <CITY>' and ends in one of three store actions (BOOK, HOLD, RSVP) through the store's WhatsApp with a property code. Use one brand handle (@westside), the app and WestStyleClub WhatsApp. Creators post on their own handles, tagged to a store.

Final architecture: 10 properties in 5 roles. SPINE: Mausam (4 issues a year, but Tyohaar is Dehleez and Shaadi is Five Functions, so only Garmi and Baarish are standalone shoots). ALWAYS-ON: The Window (weekly), The Trial Room (weekly episode plus fortnightly columns, with Style Call as the booking), Seen In (monthly per city). ROLLING: First Look (full tier and kit tier). DATED: Dehleez (Navratri to Bhai Dooj), Five Functions (Nov-Feb), Re-Edition (August). ENGINE AND COMMUNITY: The Regulars and Start Line. The 72-hour Burst and Style Call are rules and mechanics, not IPs.

Write a 52-week glass calendar now. Each store has one Window bay. In Mausam launch weeks the Window is the issue cover. In Dehleez weeks the threshold carries the festive moment and the bay stays clean. First Look and Re-Edition objects go only in that store's bay. Never stack two programmes on the same glass.

Weight the system toward the 300 mature stores, not only openings. Fashion LFL is low single digits or negative and growth is coming from new stores, so The Window, Trial Room, Seen In and Dehleez must lift existing-store footfall. First Look covers new stores.

Measure per store with real controls. Stagger every national rollout (Window, Mausam cover, Dehleez) in two waves. Use 3-5 matched control stores per test store, or a synthetic control from the network. Read festive and wedding like-for-like year on year. Pre-agree that a single store can only detect about a 10%+ lift over 4-6 weeks, so pool a city cluster. The KPI spine is footfall per store, then bookings and holds, then member-attributed bills, then ATV against walk-ins. Record Diwali 2026 and the 2026-27 wedding season per store now as baselines.

Pilot sequence. First, the next opening as First Look, with The Window, The Trial Room (4 stylists) and Seen In running for 8 weeks in that store and its city cluster against matched controls. Second, Five Functions with Bring the Card in one city cluster for the Jan-Feb 2027 wedding dates. Then Mausam No. 01 Garmi (Mar 2027), Re-Edition Vol. 01 (Aug 2027) and Dehleez Edition 01 (Diwali 2027, artist announced Aug 2027). Attempt nothing for Diwali 2026.

Make the house look Westside's, not a Zara pastiche. Keep Westside's existing wordmark. Use one uppercase sans with a serif only for numbers. Make a Devanagari or regional-script second mark the signature across every property, because Zara cannot own it. Three declared colours per Mausam issue; no price, offer or call to action on hero assets; full magazine credits including store staff by name. Hire one external photographer, stylist and art director under Umashan Naidoo for at least four issues.

Cap production at what an agency can run weekly with Westside teams. Weekly: one Window still and loop shot in the reference store, and one Trial Room episode. Fortnightly: four columns. Monthly: Seen In per city and one Regulars brief. Quarterly: Mausam stills. Per opening: a kit. Two films a year. No cinema-crew serials, monthly label films, routine livestreams or certified races in year one.

Get the humour and Target-style scale through The Regulars, not brand production. 'Bas dekh rahe hain' and The Bench become a monthly creator brief and a pilot-store fixture, scored on store-tagged UGC and bills, not shares.

Build the operations before the content. Run one WhatsApp Business provider with per-store routing and property codes rather than 311 unmanaged numbers. Show live stock per store before sending anyone. Set a hold and booking SLA. Train one stylist per new-format store. Get releases, fees and guardian consent for every member filmed. Build ASCI disclosure into every creator template. Get mall approval for floor graphics and early access.

Clean up precedents before the deck. Strip every Target claim until it has a dated URL. Fix the Zara overstatements: Studio team since 2016; 'each drop premieres in a room'; SRPLS is not weekly; SS25 cast models; the Streaming causation; the Athleticz curator backlash. Re-check Zara India for a Diwali 2026 drop before claiming the festive calendar is open. Correct the 11.85M WhatsApp mislabel and the Guwahati and Gachibowli 'new store' errors. Verify the store-number rule, the founding year and archive availability.

Positioning: sell the system as Westside's own Indian calendar (seasons, thresholds, wedding cards, family), done to Zara-grade restraint. Do not sell it as 'Zara at Westside prices'. Westside loses that comparison on fashion credibility, and Trent still holds about 20% of Zara India.

research.summary:
Zara runs its content as a set of named, numbered properties that work like magazine franchises, not as one-off ads. Each has a name, an edition or volume number, a season, a fixed creative crew with public credits, and a short physical premiere before it rolls out to selected stores and the app.

The examples: ZARA ORIGINS (15 Sep 2021, 205 pieces, own M/M Paris typeface and symbols, a commissioned soundtrack each edition); Zara Studio (since 2016; Meisel portraits, a Baron-directed film, Templer styling, every SS and FW); SRPLS (Nov 2018, numbered up to CLLCTN 16 in Apr 2026); Athleticz (30 Sep 2021, launched with playlists; a runner "curator" in 2026); Zara Man's in-house strands ("New Gen", "Archive", "Evening Edition"); Zara Home designer series (Van Duysen Collection 01-04; Baisi Guadagnino "Atlas of Desire" on 26 Sep 2026 with a Milan pop-up and a Guadagnino film); Zara Beauty (12 May 2021, Diane Kendal, Baron films, "There is no beauty, only beauties"); Zara Kids (rotating photographers, Kids Studio SS26 by Koto Bolofo, Caramel London from 3 Jun 2026, and an India kidswear capsule in Apr 2026); the 50th anniversary (a Meisel film of 50 models on 9 May 2025, then "50 Creators" objects at $70-3,500 with a George V pop-up on 2-5 Oct 2025); and a rolling run of collaborations.

The collaborations include Ader Error, Narciso Rodriguez, Kaia Gerber, Meisel NY, Pilati, Jayesh Sachdev's Diwali "Reverie" (Zara's first India collaboration, with a tiger sculpture at Phoenix Palladium Mumbai), Kate Moss x2, SR_A, Soshiotsuki, Willy Chavarria's "Vatisimo" telenovela film (26 Mar 2026), Bad Bunny's "BENITO ANTONIO" (seeded at the Super Bowl and Met Gala, out 21 May 2026), and Galliano's Re{form} Vol. 1 (announced 17 Mar 2026, out 1 Oct 2026; 157 items at $29.99-999.99, Meisel portraits, a by-appointment hotel particulier in the Marais).

Editorial and live: a magazine-style website (2022), Wallpaper* travel books (Apr 2023), Guadagnino's 43-minute "O Night Divine" (Dec 2021), and "The Fold-er", a shoppable columnist section in the app (Jun 2026). Zara Streaming ran inside Zara's own app: Douyin first (Nov 2023; 50% more products sold out in Q1 2024), then three Western episodes (Sep 2024 to Apr 2025) hosted by Crawford and Gerber. No 2026 episode was found.

The look comes from a small, stable crew: Baron & Baron (which also designed the 2019 logo), Meisel, Templer (creative director of SRPLS), Craig McDean, Pat McGrath and Guido Palau, plus in-house editors Gorka Sorozabal and Juan Medina. Results are mostly anecdotal sell-outs (the Galliano neckerchief gone by 09:45; Bad Bunny caps in minutes). Inditex's H1 2026 shows Zara at EUR 13.78bn (about +4.8%).

For Westside: make "Seen at Westside" a numbered, crew-credited, store-premiered system with one house look. WebFetch was blocked, so every finding comes from search-result text. Full notes: /home/user/INDULGE/research_notes/Zara and Target content IP/zara_content_properties.md

ips.name: ZARA ORIGINS
ips.what: A permanent premium menswear wardrobe line released in numbered 'editions'. Each edition has its own film, soundtrack and graphic identity, apart from the main Zara feed.
ips.launched: Unveiled 15 Sep 2021 after two years of development: 205 pieces, online plus 39 international stores. Pop-up at 40 rue de Richelieu, Paris, 27 Sep-5 Oct 2021 (PFW).
ips.format: Edition film plus stills and lookbook. Edition 1: Bryan Senti's orchestral 'Avril 14th' (Aphex Twin) film, directed by Roger Guardia, shot in a swimming pool. Edition 2 (SS22): Bob Marley 'Sun is Shining' mixed-media project. Edition 3 (Winter 2022): creative director Bynt, 'Autumn' soundtrack by Aoki Takamasa.
ips.cadence: Became year-round essentials topped up by limited seasonal pieces. SS and FW campaigns: 2024 and SS25 by Bynt, FW25 by Valentin Hennequin and Juan Medina, FW26 with Jegor Venned (Aug 2026).
ips.channels: zara.com and the app (Origins section), Instagram, Paris pop-up, a dedicated central zone on the Champs-Elysees flagship men's floor.
ips.art_direction: M/M Paris designed a separate graphic identity for edition 3: a new typeface and seven symbols ('imagotypes') applied to branding and garments. Muted neutral palettes declared per season (SS22: indigo, fuchsia, lilac over ecru, beige, navy; FW26: indigo, navy, brown, cream). Male casting with an editorial, gallery feel. Music-led film rather than product demos.
ips.why_it_works: A sub-brand with its own typeface, symbols and soundtrack reads as a label, not a price tier. Premiering in Paris during fashion week frames basics as fashion. Edition numbering gives the press a story every season.
ips.results: No sales figures found.
ips.westside_lesson: Give one Westside men's label (E.T.A. or KALA by E.T.A.) an 'Edition 01' system: a small typeface and symbol set, one commissioned soundtrack, and a one-store premiere styled as an exhibition. Then number every season.

ips.name: Zara Studio Collection (and its campaign films)
ips.brand: Zara Woman / Man / Kids (premium seasonal line)
ips.what: Zara's premium seasonal collection and its flagship image-maker. Each season gets a Steven Meisel portrait campaign and a short film by Fabien Baron.
ips.launched: Introduced as a premium capsule for fall 2016. Latest: SS26 press release 20 Mar 2026.
ips.format: Stills plus a short film, a different film genre each season. SS22: painted and digital moving portraits. FW22: urban exterior short. SS23: split-screen portraits with spoken-word voiceover; men's in sci-fi-teaser style. FW24: black-and-white portraits flashing on a digital billboard on a semi truck in an alpine desert. SS25 'On the Road': Avedon-like black-and-white portraits. FW25 'Whispers of the Wild': New York mansion gardens. SS26: 'faded and domestic' romance.
ips.cadence: Twice a year (SS, FW), always with the same core team.
ips.channels: zara.com and the app hero, Instagram, out-of-home (the FW24 billboard concept), selected stores.
ips.art_direction: Meisel shoots womenswear, Baron & Baron and Fabien Baron do creative direction and the films, Karl Templer styles and creative-directs, Pat McGrath does make-up and Guido Palau hair. Mostly black-and-white or desaturated studio or single-location portraits. A mix of established and fresh models (SS26: Hejia Li, Lauren Huyskens, Libby Taverner, Luna Yohannan, Malin Rudnick). Seasonal palette named (SS26: powder blue, sage, blush). SS26 also had kidswear by Koto Bolofo and menswear by Mark Kean. The images carry no price or offer.
ips.why_it_works: It uses the same photographer, stylist and art director as luxury houses, in the same visual language, so fashion media review it like a luxury campaign (The Impression, Fashion Gone Rogue). The fixed team makes every season recognisably 'Zara' while the genre changes.
ips.results: No campaign metrics found. Coverage reads like reviews of fashion work.
ips.westside_lesson: Pick one Westside house team (photographer, stylist, art director) and keep them for at least four seasons on one hero line. Change the film genre each season, but never the team, the typography or the no-price rule.

ips.name: SRPLS
ips.what: A utilitarian, military-surplus-inspired line ('beautility') released as numbered collections in two drops.
ips.launched: Nov 2018: online only, weekly drops from 15 Nov, 50 pieces, GBP 19.99-400, XXS-XXL for men and women.
ips.format: Numbered 'CLLCTN' releases (CLLCTN 02 in Spring 2019 up to CLLCTN 16 in Apr 2026), each with a lookbook campaign. Drop 1 and Drop 2 a week apart.
ips.cadence: Twice a year. FW24 (13th): 7 and 14 Nov 2024 at $27.90-329. SS26 (16th): April 2026, second drop 16 Apr.
ips.channels: zara.com and the app, selected stores, Instagram.
ips.art_direction: Karl Templer is creative director for SRPLS ('oversees the entire creative vision', his site). Craig McDean is the recurring photographer (SS19, FW22, SS23, SS24, FW24). Khaki, black, green and earth tones; SS26 adds wider colour with washed finishes. Clean, functional styling.
ips.why_it_works: Numbering makes it collectible and reportable ('the 16th collection'). A fixed creative director plus photographer gives it consistency across eight years. Drops create urgency without discounting.
ips.results: No sales data found. Longevity (16 collections in about 7.5 years) is the visible signal.
ips.westside_lesson: Run 'The Window' (the weekly Friday mannequin drop) as a numbered series ('Window No. 001...'). Keep one stylist as its credited creative director and one photographer, so the archive becomes a collectible run.

ips.name: Zara Athleticz
ips.what: A sportswear sub-line with its own logo and online section. It launched with lifestyle content (playlists, reportedly healthy recipes) and has added running and padel partners and a runner 'curator'.
ips.format: Product line plus lifestyle content (two playlists at launch). Partner capsules: Joma sneakers (Nov 2021), NOX padel (undated), Ridar running (2026). Local activation 'Ordinary Heroes': a hand-painted football pitch in Shoreditch with local athletes (date unverified).
ips.cadence: Seasonal. A trail range in Jun 2024; the 'Athleticz + Ridar 26' campaign in Sep 2026.
ips.channels: zara.com Athleticz section, Instagram, out-of-home and street activation.
ips.art_direction: In-house editorial: the Ridar 26 campaign was shot by James Brodribb, creative director Gorka Sorozabal, styled by Ruben Vazquez. Outdoor and trail settings, athlete casting.
ips.why_it_works: Content about the activity (music, food, community) rather than the garment. A credible figure from the sport (ultrarunner Patrick Stangbye named 'curator', reported Oct 2026) lends authenticity, though it caused backlash.
ips.results: No sales data. The curator appointment drew critical reaction from the running community (Substack, Marathon Handbook).
ips.westside_lesson: Wesness is already Westside's Athleticz advantage. Name a Wesness run captain as credited 'curator' of a run capsule, publish run playlists, and start each Saturday run at a store with a numbered route card.

ips.name: Zara Man editorial strands
ips.what: Named, recurring in-house editorial formats plus designer menswear capsules and a men-only pop-up store.
ips.launched: Heritage campaigns go back to David Sims (SS2011, Jamie Dornan). 2025-26 named strands: 'Selected by' (Jul 2025), 'Speed Run' (Nov 2025), 'Studio Party Collection' (Dec 2025), 'New Gen' SS26 (Feb 2026), 'ZARA MAN ARCHIVE SS26', 'Evening Edition SS2026' (5 Apr 2026), FW26 lookbook.
ips.format: Editorial lookbooks and short-form video. Designer capsules: Studio Nicholson (12 Sep 2022; Nov 2023 with a Seoul pop-up), SR_A by Samuel Ross (Feb 2025 and Oct 2025).
ips.cadence: Several named drops per season.
ips.channels: zara.com Man section, a separate @zaraman Instagram (launch date unclear), Zara Man pop-up at 73 Spring St, SoHo (26 Mar to about June 2026, boutique-style with less product density and more personal attention).
ips.art_direction: In-house creative direction by Gorka Sorozabal and Juan Medina. A consistent photographer per strand (Alvaro Perena Jimenez for Archive, Evening Edition, Sunglasses and FW26). Soft natural light on raw concrete, urban streets and autumn woods. Relaxed, 'worn not performed' styling.
ips.why_it_works: Named strands make routine product drops feel like magazine features. A low-cost in-house team holds the house look without a star photographer.
ips.results: None found.
ips.westside_lesson: Give E.T.A. three named in-house strands ('Office Edition', 'Wedding Guest Edition', 'Archive'), each with one fixed photographer and one look. Shoot them in a Westside store and credit everyone.

ips.name: Zara Home designer editions (Kassl, Vincent Van Duysen, Baisi Guadagnino) and The Apartment
ips.what: Designer and architect series presented like design-magazine stories, plus an apartment-style retail concept.
ips.launched: Kassl Editions in Sep 2021. Van Duysen Collection 01 on 30 Jun 2022 (19 pieces), then dining, then Collection 04 (revealed about 12 Jun 2025, shot in the Mies van der Rohe Pavilion, Barcelona). 'The Apartment' flagship at 117 rue du Bac, Paris (23 May 2024, 1,600 m2, for one year). Baisi Guadagnino 'Atlas of Desire': 200+ pieces on 26 Sep 2026, with a La Pelota Milan pop-up on 26-27 Sep.
ips.format: Numbered designer collections, location shoots in architectural landmarks, brand films (SS25 Riviera film by Animal / Nest Productions), and a Guadagnino-directed short written by Scott Z. Burns for Atlas of Desire.
ips.cadence: About one major designer chapter a year, plus seasonal campaigns.
ips.channels: zarahome.com, zara.com (Atlas of Desire includes ready-to-wear), selected stores, Milan and Paris pop-ups, design press (Wallpaper*, Domus, Dezeen).
ips.art_direction: Architecture as backdrop (the Mies Pavilion), cinematic interiors, warm natural light, references to design history named in the press (Viennese Secession, French Art Deco, Brazilian Modernism, Italian Radical Design). Designer voice quoted ('This ongoing collection reflects 30 years of my work').
ips.why_it_works: Design press covers it as design news. Named designers and numbered collections give it collectible status. Room sets sell a life rather than items.
ips.results: No sales figures found.
ips.westside_lesson: Build a Westside Home 'Edition 01' with one Indian designer. Shoot it in a real Indian home or landmark interior, number it, and premiere it as an apartment-style room set inside one new store.

ips.name: Zara Beauty
ips.what: Zara's make-up line, launched with a celebrity make-up-artist creative director, an art-film campaign and a manifesto line.
ips.launched: 12 May 2021: 130 shades in matte, satin and pearl, refillable cases. Skin collection 21 Mar 2022: foundation in 51 shades, concealer in 36.
ips.format: 'The Call' short-film series by Fabien Baron. 'On the Line' story by Craig McDean. A 2022 portrait campaign by Tyler Mitchell with contrasting shadows across skin tones.
ips.cadence: Launch-led. No 2025-26 campaign found.
ips.channels: zara.com and the app, selected stores, Instagram.
ips.art_direction: Creative direction by Fabien Baron and Christophe Derigon (Baron & Baron). Diane Kendal is creative director of the line. Graphic black liner, close-crop faces, varied casting. Manifesto: 'There is no beauty, only beauties.'
ips.why_it_works: Make-up-artist authorship and a manifesto make a high-street launch read like an artistry brand. Shade-range portraits make inclusivity the visual.
ips.results: Hola headline (Mar 2022) claimed record shade breadth (51 shades, more than Fenty). No sales data.
ips.westside_lesson: Relaunch Studiowest with a one-line manifesto and a named Indian make-up artist as credited creative director. Run a shade-range portrait series shot on real WestStyleClub members.

ips.name: Zara Kids (incl. Kids Studio and kids collaborations)
ips.what: Seasonal kidswear campaigns with a rotating roster of art photographers, a premium Kids Studio line, and multi-season label collaborations.
ips.launched: Photographers by season: Tyler Mitchell (spring 2021), Nagi Sakai (fall 2021), William Arcand (spring 2022), Nick Dorey (winter 2022), Marcin Kempski (summer 2023), Hart Leshkina (SS25), Koto Bolofo (Kids Studio SS26, Apr 2026). Collaborations: Sea (likely Jul 2024), Closed (Feb 2025, girls 6-14, EUR 15.95-55.95), Soshiotsuki (4 Dec 2025), Caramel London (multi-season from 3 Jun 2026, with an Osaka corner by Profirst). India: 'Curated At Home' limited kidswear capsule (Mumbai, Apr 2026).
ips.format: Stills plus short films. A 60-second back-to-school dance film by D+Y with DONTSTOP DANCE (Shots, 21 Sep 2026, single source).
ips.cadence: SS, FW and back-to-school, plus about two collaborations a year.
ips.channels: zara.com Kids, the @zarakids Instagram (about 2.6M, third-party estimate), selected stores and in-store corners.
ips.art_direction: Candid moments, natural light, rustic stucco walls and ivy, Mediterranean summer mood, earthy tones (Kids Studio SS26, styled by Templer). Child-led movement in films.
ips.why_it_works: Art-photographer authorship and candid realism avoid the 'catalogue kid' look. Collaborations with niche parents' labels (Caramel, Closed) borrow taste.
ips.results: None found.
ips.westside_lesson: Shoot Westside kids content the Zara Kids way: natural light, real families, candid, one credited photographer per season. Pair it with a back-to-school dance film made with a local kids' dance school that performs in-store on launch day.

ips.name: 50 Years, 50 Icons (anniversary film and tuxedo capsule)
ips.what: A birthday tentpole: a Steven Meisel film of 50 models lip-syncing Donna Summer's 'I Feel Love', a black-and-white tuxedo capsule, and a redesign of the first store.
ips.launched: 9 May 2025, exactly 50 years after the first store opened on Calle Juan Florez, A Coruna.
ips.format: Music film plus portraits plus a capsule of 128 pieces (Refinery29) or 150 (W). The A Coruna first store was redesigned alongside it.
ips.cadence: One-off anniversary, but uses the founding date as an owned date.
ips.channels: zara.com and the app, Instagram, global stores, press exclusive (WWD).
ips.art_direction: Monochrome tuxedo dressing, a 'seductive palette of black', styled by Karl Templer, beauty by Pat McGrath and Guido Palau. A cross-generational supermodel cast (Twiggy, Naomi Campbell, Cindy Crawford, Christy Turlington to Lina Zhang). Lip-sync performance rather than product demo.
ips.why_it_works: The cast is the news. One song, one colour and one garment type make it instantly legible. Tying it to the founding store gives the brand a myth.
ips.results: No commercial figures found.
ips.westside_lesson: Turn Westside's founding date and first store into an annual owned day (founding year reportedly 1998, to verify). Make one film with 30 real customers and staff across generations, one song, one colour, one garment type.

ips.name: 50 Creators (50th-anniversary 'objects of desire')
ips.what: Marta Ortega asked 50 cultural figures, from fashion, music, film, photography, architecture and design, each to make one 'object of desire'. It was sold as a charity capsule.
ips.launched: Announced 29-30 Sep 2025. Paris pop-up and exhibition at 40 avenue George V, 2-5 Oct 2025, curated by Sarah Andelman. On sale in stores and on zara.com from 6 Oct 2025.
ips.format: Exhibition-style pop-up plus a collectible product range ($70-3,500). Examples: Meisel pet carrier, Rosalia 'Conversation Island' sofa (about $3,500), Naomi Campbell biker dress ($529), Ludovic de Saint Sernin chair ($2,299), Pat McGrath make-up bag; also Almodovar, Guadagnino, Piccioli, Marc Newson, Norman Foster, Es Devlin, Kate Moss.
ips.cadence: One-off.
ips.channels: Paris pop-up, zara.com, selected stores, global press (Dezeen, W, Nylon).
ips.art_direction: Each creator's own authorship. Exhibition display rather than retail racks.
ips.why_it_works: Fifty names produce fifty press stories, each across a different media vertical (design, music, film). Charity profits (Women's Earth Alliance and others) remove the hard-sell tone.
ips.results: No sales or donation totals found. One source says some items were pop-up-exclusive.
ips.westside_lesson: FRONT ROW already has 150 culture-shapers. Ask 30 of them for one 'object of desire' each, show them as a one-week exhibition in a flagship store, and sell with profits to a named cause.

ips.name: Re{form} Zara by John Galliano
ips.what: A two-year partnership in which Galliano deconstructs and rebuilds garments from Zara's own past seasons into seasonal volumes.
ips.launched: Announced 17-18 Mar 2026. Vol. 1 revealed 30 Sep 2026 (PFW), on sale 1 Oct 2026 at 10:00 CEST.
ips.format: Volumes (Vol. 1: 35 looks, 157 items, $29.99-999.99). Meisel studio portrait campaign. By-appointment installation at a hotel particulier, 70 rue des Archives, Marais, 1-6 Oct 2026, booked via zara.com.
ips.cadence: Seasonal volumes over two years.
ips.channels: zara.com in nine countries, Madrid and London flagships (some reports say wider), Paris installation, global press.
ips.art_direction: Steven Meisel portraits in the studio. Karl Templer styling, Stephen Jones hats, Guido Palau hair, Pat McGrath make-up, casting by Piergiorgio Del Moro. Seven models in black looks. Les Incroyables and Les Merveilleuses theme, echoing Galliano's 1984 graduate collection.
ips.why_it_works: Uses the brand's own archive as raw material, so the story is about Zara. Volume numbering promises a sequel. Flagship-only and appointment access create scarcity.
ips.results: Anecdotal: a gingham neckerchief sold out in every colour by 09:45 on launch day; store lines and an online rush (Brazilian press). Critics split (theFashionSpot forum called the images 'flat'). No Inditex numbers yet.
ips.westside_lesson: Run 'Westside Re-Edition': a known Indian designer reworks archive Westside own-label pieces into 'Vol. 01'. Sell it only in the next new store, shown by appointment for its first three days.

ips.name: Willy Chavarria 'Vatisimo'
ips.what: A designer capsule launched with a telenovela-style short film. The name comes from the Chicano slang 'vato', and the capsule celebrates friendship.
ips.launched: 26 Mar 2026: NY pop-up at 73 Spring St, selected stores worldwide and zara.com.
ips.format: Short film co-directed by Chavarria and Glen Luchford, starring Christy Turlington and Alberto Guerra, shot in Mexico in a retro Mexico City mansion. Product at $25-529.
ips.cadence: One-off capsule.
ips.channels: SoHo pop-up (later a Zara Man store until about June), zara.com, Instagram, press.
ips.art_direction: Telenovela melodrama (a 'fatal love quadrangle'), saturated retro interiors, a supermodel lead, the designer as co-director.
ips.why_it_works: A genre film with a plot gets watched and written about. It isn't scrolled past as an ad. The designer's identity story gives it meaning beyond product.
ips.results: None found.
ips.westside_lesson: Make the festive film the Westside never made: a 6-episode Hindi-soap-style mini-drama set in a Westside store (the trial room as the stage), released one episode a day before Diwali.

ips.name: Kate Moss for Zara (two editions)
ips.what: Celebrity-authored capsules drawn from Moss's own wardrobe: a party capsule with stylist Katy England, then a festival capsule with Bobby Gillespie designing menswear.
ips.format: Campaign stills plus a Super 8 video (edition 2).
ips.cadence: Seasonal editions, timed to party season and then festival season.
ips.channels: zara.com, selected stores, Instagram, press.
ips.art_direction: Mert Alas and Marcus Piggott photographed both editions, with Baron & Baron and Fabien Baron on creative direction. Hair by Paul Hanlon, make-up by Isamaya Ffrench (edition 1). 1970s and disco references, leopard, bias-cut tea dresses; rock-and-roll for edition 2.
ips.why_it_works: Authentic authorship (her real stylist, her real partner, her favourite photographers) makes it read as her wardrobe rather than a licensing deal. The edition structure lets the press frame edition 2 as 'the return'.
ips.results: Distribution of 120+ locations for edition 2. No sales data.
ips.westside_lesson: Use a celebrity's real circle: their real stylist co-designs, a real occasion (sangeet, festival) sets the season, and the edition number tells the story ('Edition 02: the wedding season').

ips.name: Bad Bunny 'BENITO ANTONIO'
ips.what: A 150-piece collaboration seeded months ahead through Bad Bunny wearing custom Zara on the biggest stages, with a hometown preview pop-up.
ips.launched: Custom Zara at the Super Bowl LX halftime show (8 Feb 2026), a Zara-designed tuxedo at the Met Gala (4 May), a preview pop-up at Plaza Las Americas, Puerto Rico (16 May, with a surprise appearance), global on 21 May 2026.
ips.format: Seeding through live culture moments, then a pop-up, then a global drop. Co-created with his creative director Janthony Oliveras.
ips.cadence: One-off.
ips.channels: Live TV moments, social, the Puerto Rico pop-up, zara.com, selected stores (fewer than 40 US stores).
ips.art_direction: A Caribbean palette of whites, pastel yellow and coral pink. Tailoring and oversized basics from his personal style.
ips.why_it_works: Wearing the clothes before announcing them turns the reveal into a story. The hometown premiere gives the launch authenticity and viral footage.
ips.results: Anecdotal: caps and bandanas sold out within minutes online, quiet restocks, hundreds queuing in Barcelona.
ips.westside_lesson: Seed before you sell. Dress a FRONT ROW culture-shaper in a custom Westside look at a big live moment (an IPL final, an award show), reveal it was Westside, then open a hometown preview store with them in it.

ips.name: Designer-archive and cult-label collaborations (Ader Error, Narciso Rodriguez, Kaia Gerber, Steven Meisel NY, Harry Lambert, Stefano Pilati, SR_A by Samuel Ross, Soshiotsuki, Caramel London)
ips.what: A continuous run of named capsules, about four to six a year, each with a famous-photographer campaign and often a pop-up.
ips.launched: Ader Error AZ Collection (6 Dec 2021; Zepeto metaverse; edition 2 Dec 2022 with Seoul and Paris pop-ups). NYC Ballet with Vanessa Beecroft (Jan 2022). Narciso Rodriguez (8 Sep 2022). Kaia Gerber (4 Oct 2022). Steven Meisel New York (18 Sep 2023; pop-ups at 33 Howard St and Dover Street Market). Harry Lambert 'Cutie Chaos' (13 Nov 2023). Stefano Pilati (3 Oct 2024). SR_A (6 Feb 2025; Season 2 Oct 2025). Soshiotsuki (4 Dec 2025). Caramel London (3 Jun 2026).
ips.format: Capsule plus portrait campaign, plus pop-up or party in a fashion capital.
ips.cadence: Continuous. Multi-season deals (SR_A, Caramel, Galliano) are increasingly favoured.
ips.channels: zara.com and the app, selected stores, pop-ups (Paris, New York, Seoul, London), press.
ips.art_direction: Narciso: Natalia Vodianova shot by Craig McDean, studio portraits with supports retouched out so she floats. Kaia: black-and-white by Fabien Baron. Pilati: Meisel black-and-white in New York with Pilati and Gisele. Meisel NY: portraits of 26 supermodels. SR_A: Gabriel Moses with Jules Kounde, then Willy Vanderperre outdoors. Lambert: Mark Kean on a pink seamless backdrop.
ips.why_it_works: Each capsule borrows a designer's archive or cult credibility and gets a luxury-grade photographer. Collaboration becomes the editorial calendar, so press coverage is continuous without paid media.
ips.results: Mostly qualitative. Ader Error sold in about 10 countries. No sales data found.
ips.westside_lesson: Run a published annual collaboration calendar: four Indian designer or label capsules a year (e.g. with YNG/NIFT alumni). Give each a credited photographer, a one-store premiere and a number.

ips.name: Zara x Jayesh Sachdev 'Reverie' (Diwali, India)
ips.what: Zara's first India collaboration: a Diwali capsule by artist Jayesh Sachdev (Quirk Box), anchored by a giant in-store sculpture.
ips.format: Capsule (tees, sweatshirts, totes, patchouli candles) for women, men and kids. A 10-foot tiger sculpture at the Phoenix Palladium flagship in Mumbai, and special corners in New Delhi, Bengaluru, Pune and Gurugram.
ips.cadence: One-off (no 2025 Diwali sequel found).
ips.channels: Selected India stores, zara.com/in, Indian trade and lifestyle press.
ips.art_direction: Festive icons (diyas, fireworks, lanterns) in Sachdev's eclectic style. The sculpture is the photo moment.
ips.why_it_works: One giant, photographable store object gives social a reason to visit the store. A local artist gives local relevance.
ips.results: None found.
ips.westside_lesson: Westside can make this an annual Diwali tradition Zara dropped: a named artist each year, one giant photographable installation in every new-format store, and a numbered 'Diwali Edition'.

ips.name: Zara editorial and journal: magazine-style website, Wallpaper* books, 'O Night Divine', The Fold-er
ips.what: Zara's own publishing layer: a magazine-style site, a box set of travel photo books, a long-form Christmas film, and from June 2026 a shoppable columnist section in the app.
ips.launched: Website editorial push reported Jan 2022 (Meisel, Baron, Templer, Guadagnino). 'O Night Divine' by Luca Guadagnino, Dec 2021 (about 43 min; John C. Reilly, Alex Wolff; score by Alberto Iglesias). Wallpaper* 'Where to now', Apr 2023 (five photo books: Bruton, Ojai, Galicia, Naoshima, Windhoek; EUR 79.95). 'The Fold-er', Jun 2026: columns by Leandra Medine, Arielle Charnas, Manon De Velder and Laura Roso Vidrequin.
ips.format: Columns of text and photos, each with a shoppable edit. Printed books. A long-form film. Exhibitions (Meisel '1993' in A Coruna, 19 Nov 2022-1 May 2023, MOP Foundation).
ips.cadence: The Fold-er is a recurring section (seasonal columns). The others are one-offs.
ips.channels: zara.com and the app (The Fold-er sits in womenswear), Zara-sold books, YouTube and film channels.
ips.art_direction: Magazine layouts in the site and app. Columnist voices and photos. Film-festival production values.
ips.why_it_works: Owned editorial keeps attention inside Zara's own app, where it converts. Named columnists give it a personality without handing the brand feed to influencers.
ips.results: None found.
ips.westside_lesson: Turn 'The Style Collective' into Westside's Fold-er: four named local stylists each write a fortnightly column inside the Westside app or WestStyleClub, each ending in a shoppable edit plus a 'book me at [store]' Style Call link.

ips.name: Zara Streaming (in-app live shopping)
ips.what: Live shopping shows: weekly on Douyin in China, then director-made episodes with supermodel hosts streamed inside Zara's own app and website in the West.
ips.launched: China: Nov 2023 (weekly, five hours, about 800,000 unique viewers per show). West: episode 1 on 25 Sep 2024 (Cindy Crawford and Kaia Gerber, powered by Bambuser), episode 2 on 27 Mar 2025, episode 3 'The Vacation Edit' on 30 Apr 2025 (with Evan Ross Katz).
ips.format: 45-60 minute shoppable live show, then on demand. Limited-edition items buyable in real time. The Bambuser release credits direction to David Lowery and styling to Carlyne Cerf de Dudzeele.
ips.cadence: Intended to be weekly in the West. Scaled back after the first episode (FashionUnited ES). No 2026 episode found.
ips.channels: Zara app and zara.com (owned, not third-party), Douyin in China.
ips.art_direction: Film-director production, supermodel family hosts, editorial styling, rather than a QVC-style presenter desk.
ips.why_it_works: Keeping the stream on owned channels kept control of the look and the checkout. Celebrity hosts and named directors made live commerce feel like an event.
ips.results: China: 50% more products sold out in most sizes in Q1 2024 than in Q1 2023 (EDITED data via Reuters). No Western metrics found.
ips.westside_lesson: Don't copy the expensive spectacle that Zara itself slowed down. 'Style Call' (one-to-one WhatsApp video styling booked into a named store) is the scalable, intimate version. Measure it on store visits booked.

ips.name: The house creative system (Baron & Baron, Steven Meisel, Karl Templer, Craig McDean and others)
ips.what: A small, stable roster of top-tier image-makers used across every property. This is the 'look' that turns the properties into one IP family.
ips.launched: Baron & Baron logo in Jan 2019 (overlapping letters, curved Z and R legs, a Harper's Bazaar echo; widely criticised, e.g. Erik Spiekermann). Meisel on Zara women's campaigns from at least FW18-19. Marta Ortega Inditex chair since Apr 2022.
ips.format: Recurring roles. Fabien Baron: creative direction and films. Meisel: womenswear portraits and special projects. Templer: styling, Studio creative director, SRPLS creative director. McDean: SRPLS, Beauty, Narciso, SS20 men. Pat McGrath and Guido Palau: beauty. Guest photographers per property (Mert & Marcus, Tyler Mitchell, Koto Bolofo, Mark Kean, Gabriel Moses, Willy Vanderperre, Paolo Roversi, Tim Walker). In-house editors Gorka Sorozabal and Juan Medina for Man, Origins and Athleticz.
ips.cadence: Continuous.
ips.channels: All.
ips.art_direction: Portrait-led, often black and white. Seamless studio or single strong location. Minimal copy; the wordmark is the only branding. Season palettes named. Supermodels cast next to fresh faces.
ips.why_it_works: WSJ Magazine (quoted second-hand, Aug 2021) said Zara's shoots rival Prada's in tone and pedigree, while Zara forgoes print advertising. The same names that shoot luxury make Zara read as luxury.
ips.results: Inditex H1 2026: Zara (incl. Zara Home and Lefties) EUR 13.78bn vs EUR 13.15bn (about +4.8%). @zara about 61.6M Instagram followers (HypeAuditor, undated). Not attributable to content.
ips.westside_lesson: Westside can't buy Meisel, but it can buy consistency. Keep a fixed in-house chief creative (Umashan Naidoo) and one external photographer-stylist pair for all 'Seen at Westside' properties. Publish full credits on every post.

design_lessons: Name it and number it. SRPLS CLLCTN 16, Re{form} Vol. 1, Atelier Collection 04, Van Duysen Collection 04 and SR_A Season 2 all carry numbers, which turn a drop into a series people collect and the press can count. Every 'Seen at Westside' format should carry a number (Trial Room No. 012, Window No. 047).

One house crew, many labels. A fixed core team (Baron & Baron, Meisel, Templer, McDean, McGrath, Palau) gives every property a family resemblance. Each sub-line then adds one small identity layer, such as the M/M Paris typeface and seven symbols for Origins. Westside: one fixed photographer-stylist-art director pair across all IPs, plus a mini-identity per IP.

Portrait first, product second. The hero image is a single figure on a seamless backdrop or in one strong location, often black and white, without product callouts. Shoot Trial Room and Window content as portraits, not catalogue grids.

Remove the retail noise from hero assets. Zara's top-tier images seem to carry no price, discount or call to action; the wordmark is the only branding (my reading of campaign coverage, not a full audit). Keep offers out of Westside's IP layer and put them in the CRM and WhatsApp layer.

Name the season's palette and stick to it. Zara Studio SS26 was powder blue, sage and blush; Origins FW26 was indigo, navy, brown and cream. Pick three colours per Westside drop and use them across the window, film, post and in-store signage.

Make films as genre pieces, not ad cutdowns. Zara has made a sci-fi teaser, a split-screen spoken-word film, a billboard-on-a-truck desert film, a 43-minute Christmas film, a telenovela and a Super 8 home movie. Westside's missing festive film should be a recognisable Indian genre (a soap mini-series, a wedding-video parody, a dance-off).

Music is part of the identity. Origins commissioned a reimagined Aphex Twin track, an Aoki Takamasa soundtrack and a Bob Marley project; the 50th used Donna Summer's 'I Feel Love'. Commission one original track per Westside property and reuse it as the sound in store and on Reels.

Credit everyone, like a magazine. Zara's photographer, stylist, hair, make-up and casting credits circulate in fashion media, which then reviews the work as fashion, not ads. Publish credits on every Westside post. It also turns the Style Collective stylists into names.

Premiere in a room, then roll out. Zara's examples: 40 rue de Richelieu, 40 avenue George V, 70 rue des Archives by appointment, La Pelota in Milan, 73 Spring Street, Plaza Las Americas, and the Phoenix Palladium tiger in Mumbai. Every Westside property should open as a guest-list event in one named store (First Look), which also gives Mask360 its footfall-per-store metric.

Time launches to culture, not sales. Zara has launched at Paris and Milan fashion weeks, the Super Bowl, the Met Gala, its own founding day (9 May) and Diwali (Reverie 2024). Build Westside's calendar around Indian culture weeks (Lakme Fashion Week, IPL, Durga Puja, the wedding season) and Westside's own founding day.

Seed before you sell. Bad Bunny wore Zara at the Super Bowl and the Met Gala months before the drop. Kate Moss's capsules came from her real stylist and circle. Dress FRONT ROW culture-shapers in Westside first and reveal the collection later.

Use the archive and real authorship. Narciso's archive, Galliano reworking Zara's past seasons, and the ZARA MAN ARCHIVE editorial all use the brand's own history. Westside's decades of own-label history (Bombay Paisley, Utsa, E.T.A.) are unused raw material for a 'Re-Edition'. Westside's founding year needs verifying.

Keep content inside owned channels where it converts. Zara Streaming ran in its own app rather than a third-party platform, and The Fold-er puts columnists inside the app. Westside's equivalent is WestStyleClub (11.85M members) plus WhatsApp Style Call; send IP content there, not only to Instagram.
