ips.name: Seasonal Studio campaign (grid carousel + home hero + window)
ips.what: Twice-yearly 'Zara Studio' campaign, art-directed by Fabien Baron and shot by Steven Meisel (SS25, FW25 published Oct 2025, SS26). It drives the season's Instagram carousels, the app and web home-page slider (a video-backed scrolling slider in the 2023 UXMatters audit) and, per Zara's windows team, the store windows, which are renewed with each campaign.
ips.art_direction: Rough studio portraiture (SS25 references Avedon's 'In the American West'), Karl Templer styling, plenty of white space, few or no words on the image, posted in themed runs of one model, set or palette so the grid reads like a magazine spread.
ips.why_it_works: One image system makes the brand recognisable at a glance on every surface and lets the store window act as the physical 'cover' of the same issue. Production is in-house at industrial scale ('studio bays lined up like chic factory stations').
ips.westside_lesson: Shoot one festive or seasonal 'issue' for Westside, then run the same hero frame on Instagram, the app and site home, the WestStyleClub WhatsApp header and the Friday window in the same week. 'The Window' is the window of that issue, not a separate IP.
ips.cadence: Seasonal (SS / FW), with sub-drops in between
ips.channels: Instagram feed carousels, app and web home page, store windows
ips.format: Stills carousel + short motion loops + home-page slider
ips.launched: Ongoing; Baron/Meisel Studio campaigns documented SS25, FW25, SS26
ips.results: No campaign-level metrics disclosed. @zara about 61.6M followers, 0.81% engagement (HypeAuditor, snapshot undated).

ips.name: Tentpole auteur film (anniversary / special)
ips.what: '50 Years, 50 Icons': Steven Meisel's short film released 9 May 2025, 50 years to the day after the first A Coruña store opened. Fifty models, including Naomi Campbell, Cindy Crawford, Twiggy and Vittoria Ceretti, lip-sync Donna Summer's 'I Feel Love' in a black-and-white tuxedo capsule.
ips.art_direction: Black-and-white, one song, one wardrobe, many faces. Styled by Karl Templer, make-up by Pat McGrath, hair by Guido Palau. Initiated by Marta Ortega Pérez.
ips.why_it_works: One simple, repeatable idea (everyone sings the same song) turns a corporate milestone into culture. It cuts down into dozens of single-face clips for Reels and TikTok, and it anchors a shoppable capsule.
ips.westside_lesson: Westside found no festive or wedding film in the last year. Make one per year with a single idea and a large Indian cast (for example 30 New Faces plus FRONT ROW culture-shapers), cut it into one clip per face, and sell a capsule from it.
ips.cadence: Annual or one-off tentpoles
ips.channels: Instagram, web and app, press embeds
ips.format: Short music film + capsule collection
ips.results: No view figures found.

ips.name: Zara Streaming (live show)
ips.what: Shoppable live show hosted only on Zara's own app and web, made with Bambuser. It began in China on Douyin in Nov 2023: weekly 5-hour shows averaging about 800K unique viewers. The Western version runs 45-60 minutes. Ep 1 on 25 Sep 2024 and Ep 2 on 27 Mar 2025 (a limited edition sold in real time) were hosted by Cindy Crawford and Kaia Gerber. Ep 3, 'The Vacation Edit', on 30 Apr 2025 added influencer Evan Ross Katz. All are on demand afterwards.
ips.art_direction: Directed by filmmaker David Lowery. Karl Templer creative director; Carlyne Cerf de Dudzeele and later Olivia Singer styling. Designed to look like a fashion film, not a TV shopping set.
ips.why_it_works: Keeping it on owned surfaces lets Zara control the look and send traffic to its own checkout. In China, Edited data showed 50% more products selling out in most sizes in Q1 2024 than a year earlier. In the West, FashionUnited ES called episode 2 closer to 'teletienda' (teleshopping).
ips.westside_lesson: Livestream only as an event: a store launch (First Look) or a festive drop, 45-60 minutes, with a cast and a director, hosted on Westside's app, site or WhatsApp and not on a marketplace. Close each show with a store action (reserve, Style Call slot).
ips.cadence: Irregular: 3 live episodes in 7 months (Sep 2024 to Apr 2025), none found in 2026
ips.channels: Zara app and zara.com only (Douyin in China)
ips.format: 45-60 minute shoppable live broadcast, then on demand
ips.results: China: about 800K unique viewers per show; 50% more products sold out in most sizes in Q1 2024 than Q1 2023 (Edited via Reuters). No Western sales figures disclosed.

ips.name: Holiday short film on the owned channel (Le Dîner)
ips.what: The fourth Zara Streaming episode, on 11 Dec 2025, was not live shopping. It was 'Le Dîner', a roughly 15-minute Christmas film premiered at 20:00 in the Zara app and online, then on social. Social posts said 'Watch the full short movie at zara.com or on our app'.
ips.art_direction: Cinema rather than an ad. Produced by Little Spain, directed by Santos Bacana and Rogelio González. A mystery dinner in a Madrid restaurant with Rossy de Palma, Diane Kruger, Vincent Cassel, Damson Idris, Dylan Penn and Chucho Valdés, who closes the night with music.
ips.why_it_works: It gives the season's party collection a story and a reason to open the app. The full film stays on owned surfaces while short cuts travel on social.
ips.westside_lesson: For Diwali or wedding season, make one 10-15 minute film (for example a family dinner or sangeet), premiere it in the Westside app and WestStyleClub at a set hour, cut it for social, and put every outfit in it on a 'shop the film' page that also lists store stock.
ips.cadence: Seasonal (Christmas)
ips.channels: Zara app and zara.com premiere, then social
ips.format: 15-minute narrative short film
ips.results: No view figures found.

ips.westside_lesson: Give each Style Collective stylist and YNG creator a bylined column inside the Westside app and site ('The Trial Room, Vol. 1 by ...'), with photos shot in a named Westside store and buttons to book a Style Call or reserve in that store.

ips.name: Designer drop + one curated room
ips.what:

- Kate Moss debut capsule, 30 Nov 2024, campaign by Mert & Marcus.
- '50 friends of Zara' 50th-anniversary objects: Paris pop-up 2-5 Oct 2025 at 40 Avenue George V, curated by Sarah Andelman, with talks moderated by Derek Blasberg and a café by We Are Ona; launched 6 Oct 2025.

ips.cadence: Several a year; Galliano seasonal for two years from Sep/Oct 2026

ips.format: Capsule + campaign + installation (+ film or talks)

ips.name: Fit-check studio (store as a content set)
ips.what: The Nanjing 'Asia flagship' (opened 21 Mar 2025; 2,500 sq m over two floors in Xinjiekou) has a 'fit check' studio with multiple cameras and lighting settings. Customers shoot their own video and download it straight to their phones. The store also has a private shopping salon and the first Zacaffe outside Spain. The studio and salon are booked through WeChat. The features are being trialled in China before any wider rollout.

ips.westside_lesson: Put a 'Fit Check' bay next to the trial rooms of each new flagship (First Look), bookable on WhatsApp alongside Style Call. Brand the backdrop with the store's name so every clip says 'Seen at Westside, <store>', and count bookings and clips per store as a footfall measure.
ips.cadence: Always-on store feature
ips.channels: In store; booked through WeChat; output to customers' own social
ips.format: Bookable self-shoot video studio

ips.name: Zara Try-On (AI utility as content)
ips.what: An app-only AI virtual fitting feature. After a generative-AI consent notice, the user uploads a selfie and a full-body photo. Zara returns a still image and a 360-degree video of the user's avatar wearing the product, and deletes the photos after the avatar is made. It launched mid-Dec 2025 (Mexico, UK, Germany, Netherlands, Italy among the first), then Spain and the US. By 11 Mar 2026: 43 markets, more than 7M sessions, being extended to other Inditex brands.
ips.art_direction: A 'Try on' button on the product page, inside the same minimal UI. The output is a short motion clip people can share.
ips.why_it_works: A utility that produces a shareable clip and answers the 'will it suit me' question. It also keeps the person inside Zara's app.
ips.westside_lesson: Westside does not need AI first. Its equivalent is a human, store-based 'try on' (Style Call, Trial Room). Market the booking as a feature, film the results as content, and treat app or WhatsApp bookings as the KPI.
ips.cadence: Always-on
ips.channels: Zara app only
ips.format: AI avatar still + 360-degree video
ips.results: More than 7M sessions in 43 markets by FY2025 results (Inditex, 11 Mar 2026). India availability not confirmed.

ips.name: Store Mode (app to rail to fitting room)
ips.what: An in-store mode in the Zara app, launched Sept 2020 in Spain. It shows real-time stock, offers online purchase with in-store pick-up in about 30 minutes using a QR code, books a fitting-room slot (the app allocates a room and the customer has 5 minutes to claim it), and has 'Click & Find', which maps where an item sits in the store. In India, the Inorbit Mumbai store (7 Mar 2025) offers real-time inventory in the app and online pick-up in about two hours. A Travel mode was added in Jun 2025.
ips.art_direction: Utilitarian, inside the same black-and-white app UI.
ips.why_it_works: It turns the app from a catalogue into a store remote control. Content can end in 'see it, find it, try it', which is the post-to-billing-counter loop.
ips.westside_lesson: Give every piece of Westside content a store end-state: 'reserve to try at <store>', 'Style Call at <store> Saturday 4pm', 'in stock at <store>'. Build or fake this through WhatsApp and WestStyleClub before any app work.
ips.cadence: Always-on
ips.channels: Zara app in store
ips.format: In-store app utility

In Seoul, Zara Athleticz is kit partner of Lotte Department Store's 'Style Run' on 18 Oct 2026 (7,000 places, five-piece kit per runner).

ips.name: Local artist festive capsule with a store sculpture (Reverie, India)
ips.what: Zara's first India collaboration: the Diwali capsule 'Reverie' with artist Jayesh Sachdev (Quirk Box), launched 15 Oct 2024 in select Indian stores and on zara.com. It includes tees and sweatshirts for women, men and kids, totes and patchouli candles. Its centrepiece was a 10-ft tiger sculpture at the Phoenix Palladium flagship in Mumbai, with display corners in New Delhi, Bengaluru, Pune and Gurgaon.
ips.art_direction: One bold local motif (a colourful tiger, for power and protection), one large sculpture as the photo moment, small repeat corners in other cities.

Westside can own the Indian calendar: an annual festive artist capsule (Utsa, Vark) with one sculptural object per flagship that people come to photograph.

ips.name: Window as the campaign's physical cover
ips.what: Windows are renewed with each campaign and adjusted through the season to match what sells inside. HQ in A Coruña keeps full-scale pilot stores where a full-time team of architects and visual merchandisers mocks up stores and windows. One weak source says windows are photographed and sent to stores to copy on an 18-20-day cycle, and stores send photos of their layouts back. Some flagships carry video in the façade: Hong Kong has two 2560 x 8000 mm transparent LED walls looping Zara fashion video.
ips.art_direction: Minimal, campaign-matched, built centrally and reproduced locally. Motion loops where the façade allows.
ips.why_it_works: The window is the most-seen surface Zara owns: free reach on high streets and in malls that repeats the Instagram and home-page image. Central control keeps 2,000-odd stores on one look.
ips.westside_lesson: 'The Window' (weekly Friday mannequin drop) should be built centrally, photographed and posted the same morning on Instagram, the app and WhatsApp, with the store name in the caption. Flagships can add a vertical screen in the window looping the week's Reel.
ips.cadence: Per campaign; possibly an 18-20-day cycle (unverified)
ips.channels: Store windows and façades
ips.format: Centrally designed window + LED loops at flagships
ips.results: None disclosed.

design_lessons: Run one image on every surface in the same week. Zara's windows are renewed with each campaign and the campaign heads the grid and the app or web home page. Westside should launch each issue (festive, FRONT ROW, a store opening) on Instagram, the app and site home, the WestStyleClub WhatsApp header and the Friday window together, and caption it with the store's name.

Keep the brand account quiet and let creators make the noise. @zara (about 62M) posts magazine-like runs with little copy, while about 100K creator TikToks carry the hauls. Westside's main handle should look like a magazine; YNG creators and the Style Collective supply the try-on and haul volume on their own handles, tagged to stores.

Name every format, give it an author and a number. Zara uses The Fold-er (bylined columns), Zara Streaming (episodes), 'Selected By' and 'Archive S/S 26' (Zara Man), and Re{form} Vol. 1 (Galliano). Westside: 'The Trial Room, Ep. 4 at Westside Kalyani Nagar, by <stylist>', 'FRONT ROW Vol. 1', 'The Window, Week 12'.

Bring creators onto Westside's own surfaces rather than renting their feeds. The Fold-er puts influencer columns inside zara.com and the app, with a shop link under every photo, and Streaming was kept on Zara's own app 'to control aesthetics'. Host Style Collective and YNG columns in the Westside app and site, ending in Style Call and reserve-in-store buttons.

Make one long piece a year and cut it into many short ones. '50 Years, 50 Icons' (one song, 50 faces) and the roughly 15-minute 'Le Dîner' premiered on owned channels and were then cut for social. Westside has no festive or wedding film from the last year: make one with a single idea and a large Indian cast, premiere it at a set hour in the app or WhatsApp, and post one clip per face.

Only go live when it is an event. Zara's Western live shows were short (45-60 minutes), directed by a filmmaker and hosted by stars. A critic still called episode 2 teleshopping, and Zara reframed Christmas as a film. design_lessons: 1. Attribute in store, not online. About 94% of Westside's sales happen in store, so give each creator a WestStyleClub-linked code or ID that is redeemed or captured at the billing counter. Pay creators and move them up tiers on member-attributed bills, store visits and new-member sign-ups, not link clicks. An online-only affiliate model (the kind Target reportedly moved away from; unverified) would reward roughly 6% of the business.

2. Recruit from the 11.85M members first. Invite high-engagement WestStyleClub members who already post as the base tier, as an ambassador programme drawn from shoppers would. Their membership ID becomes their creator ID, which settles attribution and authenticity at once.

3. Organise creators by store catchment. Give each of the 311 stores a small local cast of three to five creators, and require every post to name the store, mall and neighbourhood. That fixes the gap where Westside's content rarely names a store, and makes footfall per store the natural metric.

4. Grow the programme with the store roll-out. Westside opens 50-100 stores a year and growth comes from new stores, so each opening (First Look) seeds a new local creator cohort. The programme then grows with the business rather than as a separate national push.

5. Use tiers whose perks happen in a store. Gamified tiers work when the rewards are scarce access, not just money: Friday Window previews, trial-room shoot slots, Style Call priority, FRONT ROW and Wesness invites, and capsule co-design for the top tier. Every perk brings a creator, and their audience, into a store.

6. Run one monthly central brief. Thousands of posts only look like one brand if there is a single brief: one hero edit, one shot grammar (trial-room frame, mirror, natural light), approved hooks, a fixed end card and a fixed store call to action. Ship it as templates, so creators keep their voice inside a Zara-grade frame.

7. End every post in a store action Westside can fulfil, the equivalent of Target's Drive Up and Order Pickup role: 'try it at [store] this weekend', 'reserve on WhatsApp', 'book a Style Call'. Use per-store WhatsApp deep links or QR codes so each action can be counted per store.

8. Make stock findable before you send people to a store. A store visit driven by content fails if the item is not there. Show stock at named stores, or use WhatsApp to confirm before the visit, in the spirit of Target's in-store aisle-locator mode, and prioritise own labels where Westside controls availability.

9. Prove it in one store or city cluster first. Pilot with one store launch or one festive drop, measured against matched control stores (footfall, bills, average transaction value, new members), before scaling to hundreds of creators, the way a pilot-then-launch model would.

10. Fold the existing communities into the tiers rather than adding a new programme. Wesness runners, YNG's 4,000 creators and FRONT ROW's 150 culture-shapers should become feeder or top tiers of the same ambassador ladder, so Westside runs one system with one ID and one brief.

11. Build a creator-to-capsule path. Give the top tier a route to co-design a limited own-label capsule, sold first in named stores with a launch-day appearance. That creates hunt-in-store urgency, as creator collections like Target's Tabitha Brown range did (2021; unverified).

12. Build in Indian compliance and festive timing. Follow ASCI's influencer disclosure guidelines (2021; labels such as #ad or #collab). Anchor the creator calendar on Diwali and wedding season with a 72-hour burst, which also fills Westside's missing festive campaign moment.

research.summary:
Zara's digital look borrows the grammar of a fashion magazine: full-bleed portrait photos and video, one oversized Didone wordmark used like a masthead, and small uppercase black-on-white text in a grotesque face. There is almost no colour, no rounded corners, no shadows and no promotional clutter. UXMatters (Sep 2023) says the home page is a video slider that puts looks ahead of usability. Pixc says the pages have lots of white space and are 'not immediately bombarded with products and promotions'. TheIndustry.fashion (Jan 2022) reports that Zara brought zara.com closer to fashion-magazine looks with Meisel, Baron, Templer and Guadagnino.

The logo is well documented. Baron & Baron redrew it in Jan 2019 as a high-contrast serif with overlapping letters (FashionUnited 28 Jan 2019; Dezeen 4 Feb 2019).

The UI typeface is NOT verified. From memory, it is a Neue Helvetica / Helvetica Neue-family face (medium confidence that it is in the Helvetica family, low confidence on the exact cut). I found no evidence for or against a custom 'Zara' UI face.

This run had no new web access. The first WebSearch call returned 'budget used up' (a 200-call cap shared with the sibling agents). Direct fetches were refused: 403 policy denials for zara.com, static.zara.net, fontsinuse.com, wikipedia, target.com and fonts.google.com, and DNS failures on dezeen.com and fontsinuse.com. Cited items therefore come from sibling agents' search snippets gathered earlier on 15 Oct 2026. Font licences were checked locally against npm @fontsource metadata and the Debian copyright files. Specific UI labels and sizes come from memory and are marked M-med or M-low.

Font plan for the deck: Neue Helvetica needs a commercial web licence, so use Inter Tight (OFL, ships weights 100-900) or a self-hosted Helvetica clone for UI text. The clones are TeX Gyre Heros, Nimbus Sans, FreeSans and Liberation Sans/Arimo; none of them has light weights. For the masthead, set Westside's own wordmark in Bodoni Moda (OFL, 400-900, optical-size axis). Never recreate the ZARA logo.

deck_translation: One slide = one viewport. Use height: 100svh; give the vertical container scroll-snap-type: y mandatory and each slide scroll-snap-align: start and scroll-snap-stop: always. Keyboard: ArrowUp/ArrowDown and PageUp/PageDown move a slide; Space moves forward.

Copy the app's two-axis navigation. Chapters (THE IDEA / THE IPs / THE PILOT / THE MATHS / TEAM) sit side by side in a horizontal scroll-snap-type: x container; slides inside each chapter scroll vertically. ArrowLeft/ArrowRight change chapter.

Pin a header on every slide: a 2-line hamburger (slide index), Westside's own wordmark, and on the right, text-only labels: SEARCH (opens a jump-to-slide field shown as an underlined input), CONTACT, and 'PILOT [n]' as the bag counter.

Make the masthead huge only on chapter-opener slides: Westside wordmark in Bodoni Moda, opsz 96, weight 400-500, tracking -0.05em, 40-60% of viewport width on phone. Elsewhere, shrink it to about 18-22px tall. Never draw, trace or approximate the ZARA logo.

Use one sans for all UI and text: Inter Tight 300/400/500, self-hosted woff2, font-display: swap. Fallback stack: 'TeX Gyre Heros', 'Nimbus Sans', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif. Do not embed Neue Helvetica unless the agency owns a web licence.
Set all UI type in uppercase at 11-13px with tracking +0.03 to +0.06em. Body text is sentence case at 13-15px, line-height 1.45, max 36ch. Never bold above 500.
Allow at most one headline per slide, at most 8 words: either uppercase Inter Tight 300 (28-40px phone, 56-88px desktop) or one Didone word. Most slides should carry only a label plus one sentence.
Photos go full-bleed and edge to edge with object-fit: cover. No borders, rounded corners or shadows. Supply art-directed <picture> crops for 9:16 (phone) and 16:9 (desktop) so faces are never cut.

Colour: #000 on #FFF in UI slides and #FFF on photographs. Use a 20-30% black scrim only behind text on busy images. Secondary grey #767676 (passes AA). Hairlines rgba(0,0,0,.12). Allow at most one accent, and make it Westside's own colour. No gradients as decoration.

Show the six IPs (The Trial Room, The Style Collective, The Window, Style Call, First Look, The 72-hour Burst) as a 'listing page'. Each card is 3:4 with a 0-2px gutter, an uppercase name, and a 'price line' that holds the KPI (e.g. FOOTFALL / STORE) instead of a price. Add a working 1/2/4-column density switch.

Build each IP as a 'product page': a stacked image column, then a right-hand (desktop) or below-image (phone) panel with the IP name, a one-line cadence and KPI, and a black square-cornered 'ADD TO PILOT' button. Use native <details> accordions styled like Zara links, e.g. 'FORMAT, CADENCE & ORIGIN', 'MEASUREMENT', 'IN-STORE AVAILABILITY' (which stores and cities).

Tapping ADD opens a bottom sheet: white, square corners, 1px top hairline, sliding up in 250ms. It lets the client pick options (pilot store, city, festive drop) the way Zara picks a size, and increments 'PILOT [n]' in the header.
Use the hamburger for a full-height left panel: chapter tabs across the top, then every slide title as an uppercase list. Clicking an item jumps there. This is the deck's table of contents.

Write microcopy like Zara: uppercase nouns and imperatives (ADD, VIEW ALL, BOOK, FIND IN STORE). No exclamation marks, emoji or superlatives, and no '% off' on hero slides. State numbers plainly ('311 STORES', '11.85M MEMBERS'). Write descriptions as factual sentences that start with the thing ('A weekly mannequin drop, every Friday, in every window.').

Put an editorial credit line under hero images (PHOTOGRAPHY / STYLING / LOCATION: WESTSIDE, <store>) in 10-11px uppercase grey. Zara's campaign credits circulate as fashion work, and this is what makes the deck read as a magazine.

Video slides use autoplay muted loop playsinline with a poster frame and a small uppercase 'SOUND ON' toggle. Hold a 2-3 second still on the poster for reduced-motion users (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables autoplay).

Design phone-first at 390x844 and test at 360px with a 16px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll outside the chapter scroller. On desktop, keep the same slides full-bleed at 16:9 with the info panel on the right.

Add one deliberate 'Target contrast' slide in sentence case, bold, red and rounded, to show the alternative the pitch is rejecting. Keep every other slide in the Zara grammar so the system stays one house look.

Put a legal line in the speaker notes and the footer: 'UI grammar inspired by fashion retail apps; not affiliated with Zara/Inditex or Target.' Use no Zara or Target logos, product photos or screenshots on deck slides except in a clearly labelled reference slide.

Ship the font licences with the deck. OFL-1.1 (Inter Tight, Bodoni Moda) allows embedding and self-hosting, as long as the fonts are not sold on their own. GPL-with-font-exception (FreeSans) and GUST (TeX Gyre Heros) also allow embedding in documents.

slates.lens: Zara. The brief: few but iconic, numbered properties made by one creative eye. The store and its windows act as the media. Newness comes on a fixed day, scarcity comes from limited access, and the logo leads the typography. The test for every property: what would Westside content look like if Zara's creative team ran it at Westside prices, for Indian occasions?
slates.architecture:
The slate has one house look, seven properties and two speeds.

THE HOUSE (rules that never change):
- Umashan Naidoo is house creative director. One external photographer, stylist and art director are contracted for at least four issues.
- The Westside wordmark is the masthead. Type is one uppercase sans, plus one serif used only for numbers.
- No price, offer or call to action appears on any IP image. Offers live in WestStyleClub and WhatsApp.
- Every post carries full magazine credits.
- Every frame signs off with one dateline: 'SEEN AT WESTSIDE, <STORE>, <CITY>'. The platform name becomes the caption, so every post names a store.

HERO, the spine: MAUSAM. Four numbered issues a year on India's real seasons: Garmi, Baarish, Tyohaar and Shaadi. Each issue declares three colours and one cover. The cover runs on the grid, the app home page, the WhatsApp header and all 311 windows in the same week.

HUB, always on inside each issue:
- THE WINDOW: every Friday, numbered, the street-facing cover of the issue.
- STORE No.: every opening (50-100 a year), numbered by store count.
- THE TRIAL ROOM: bylined stylist columns every fortnight.

HELP, the conversion path: THE TRIAL ROOM's booking is the one store action every property ends in. Members book a fitting or Style Call at a named store on WhatsApp, or reserve to try.

MOMENTS, scarce and dated:
- ROSHNI at Diwali, inside the Tyohaar issue.
- THE SERIAL in wedding season, inside the Shaadi issue.
- RE-EDITION in March and August, the two quietest months.

WHAT HAPPENED TO THE DRAFT IPs:
- The Trial Room is kept and absorbs The Style Collective (the bylines) and Style Call (the booking).
- The Window is kept and now numbered.
- First Look becomes STORE No.
- Style Call and the 72-hour Burst become mechanics, not properties. On launch day the brand handle posts one quiet frame per drop. Within 72 hours, YNG creators, Style Collective stylists, clipper pages and geo-paid social in each store's 5 km catchment make the noise on their own handles. This mirrors Zara's quiet brand account and loud creator layer.
- FRONT ROW is the cast bank and the seeding engine: culture-shapers wear Re-Edition and Roshni pieces before the reveal (the Bad Bunny lesson).
- Wesness runs start at the door on STORE No. opening mornings.

PILOT: one STORE No. opening that carries Window No. 001 and the first four Trial Room columns. Measure footfall per store, WhatsApp bookings and member-attributed bills against three matched control stores.

CAVEATS:
- The Target research was blocked and has no sources, so no Target precedent is cited as fact.
- Store names, store numbers and artists in titles are illustrative. Check them against Trent's store list.
- Roshni Edition 01 is realistic for Diwali 2027 (Diwali 2026 is about three weeks away).

ips.name: MAUSAM
ips.line: Four numbered issues a year on India's real seasons, shot by one house crew. One cover runs on every Westside screen and in all 311 windows in the same week.
ips.role: Hero and spine. Each issue sets the quarter's palette, cast and cover. The Window, The Trial Room and Store No. use its three colours until the next issue.
ips.precedent: Zara Studio Collection. The same Meisel, Baron & Baron, Templer, McGrath and Palau team has shot every SS and FW since 2016. The film genre changes each season, the palette is declared (SS26: powder blue, sage, blush) and no image carries a price. Zara renews its windows with each campaign, so the window is the physical cover of the same issue.
ips.format: Per issue: 12-16 portrait stills and one 45-60 second film plus 6-second loops. The film genre changes each issue (silent film, documentary, music video, home movie). The issue also ships an app and site home slider, a WhatsApp header, a window kit for 311 stores and a printed issue card for every cash desk.
ips.cadence: Quarterly, numbered (Mausam No. 01, 02, 03...): GARMI in early March, BAARISH in the first week of July, TYOHAAR in mid-September before Navratri, SHAADI in mid-November after Diwali.
ips.channels: Westside Instagram grid (a run of 6-9 frames with little or no caption), app and westside.com home, WestStyleClub WhatsApp header, all 311 store windows, the cash-desk card, and OOH only around stores opening that quarter.
ips.cast: 8-10 faces per issue: FRONT ROW's 30 New Faces, one FRONT ROW culture-shaper and two Westside store staff. Tyohaar casts three generations of one family; Shaadi casts one real couple. The same photographer, stylist and art director shoot at least four issues. Beauty is credited to Studiowest.
art_direction: Casting: one figure per frame. Each issue spans regions, ages (at least one sitter over 50) and body sizes. No catalogue smile, no hand-on-hip pose.

Set: one real Indian location per issue, shot as architecture with no added props. Garmi: a Chandigarh-style brutalist corridor. Baarish: a Mumbai stairwell in real rain. Tyohaar: a north Kolkata courtyard house. Shaadi: a Jaipur haveli at dusk.
Light: daylight only, from one direction, with the shadows kept. Baarish is shot in real overcast weather, never in a studio.
Crop: full-length or three-quarter portraits at 3:4 and 9:16, with headroom. Never cut at the hem, and never use product-detail grids on the cover.

Typography: the Westside wordmark is the masthead, top left, with 'MAUSAM No. 03 / BAARISH' below it in small uppercase sans. A hairline Devanagari मौसम is the second mark. No price, offer or call to action on any image.
Colour: three named colours are declared on the cover and reused for the window planes, the film grade and in-store signage (e.g. Baarish: slate, moss, wet sand).
ips.store_hook: The cover goes into all 311 windows on the Friday it goes live online. The app's issue page shows each look's stock at the member's home store. The WhatsApp code on the cash-desk card books a 30-minute Mausam fitting at that store.
ips.kpi: Footfall per store in issue week against the previous four weeks and a matched control set. Mausam fittings booked and attended per store. 14-day sell-through of the cover looks.
episode_examples: Mausam No. 01 / SHAADI: 'Ivory, Rust, Night'
Mausam No. 02 / GARMI: 'Linen Hours' (a heat-haze film in one Chandigarh corridor)
Mausam No. 03 / BAARISH: 'Slate, Moss, Wet Sand' (a silent film in one Mumbai stairwell)
ips.hero_visual: A woman in a slate Utsa kurta stands three-quarter length on a rain-dark Mumbai stairwell in flat grey daylight; the only graphics are the Westside wordmark top left and 'MAUSAM No. 03 / BAARISH' in small capitals beneath it.

ips.name: THE WINDOW
ips.line: Every Friday at store opening, one new numbered look goes into a dedicated window bay in all 311 stores and onto the grid at the same minute.
ips.role: Always-on hub: the weekly newness signal and the street-facing cover of the current Mausam issue. It teaches people that Westside changes on Fridays.
ips.precedent: Zara's SRPLS has run numbered releases from Nov 2018 to CLLCTN 16 (Apr 2026), with Karl Templer as credited creative director and Craig McDean as recurring photographer, so the run became collectible and countable. Zara designs its windows centrally in full-scale mock-up stores in A Coruña for local teams to copy. Its Hong Kong flagship loops campaign video on LED façades.
ips.format: One window bay per store holds 1-3 mannequins in one look family. Each look is prototyped in a central mock-up window and shipped as a kit with a photo spec. Output per week: one straight-on portrait of the window for the grid, a 9:16 reveal Reel, a vertical screen loop at flagships and a numbered card on the glass.
ips.cadence: Weekly, Friday at store opening. Numbered continuously (Window No. 001, 002...): 52 a year, gathered each quarter into a nine-frame grid.
ips.channels: 311 window bays, the Westside Instagram grid (one frame) and Stories, an app home tile, the WestStyleClub Friday WhatsApp message, and each store's Google Business Profile photo, updated the same morning.
ips.cast: Mannequins only. One window stylist dresses them as the property's credited creative director for a full year. One house photographer shoots the reference window. Store visual-merchandising teams are credited by name on their local versions.
art_direction: One own label a week, in rotation (E.T.A., Utsa, Wardrobe, LOV, Nuon, Vark, KALA): one look family, at most three mannequins.
Set: the current issue's three colours as flat plaster or paper planes, and nothing else. No SALE vinyl, festoons or props ever touch The Window bay.
The number is the only graphic: 'No. 047' in the house serif, about 30 cm high, bottom left of the glass, and repeated as the caption.
Photograph straight-on from the mall floor at eye height, symmetrical, at 3:4, from the same angle in the same reference store every week, so the archive reads as one grid.
Light: warm 3000K top light plus one side wash. No coloured gels, no LED chasers.
ips.store_hook: The window is the content. The Friday WhatsApp message reads 'No. 047 is in your window at Westside <home store> today' and offers reserve-to-try, which holds the member's size in that store until Sunday close.
ips.kpi: Friday-to-Sunday footfall per store against pre-launch weekends. 7-day sell-through of the windowed look per store. Reserve-to-try requests and pick-ups per store.
episode_examples: Window No. 001: 'Office, Monday' (E.T.A. linen suiting, three ways)
Window No. 014: 'First Rain' (Nuon raincoats in slate)
Window No. 032: 'Three Cousins, One Sangeet' (Vark)
ips.hero_visual: A three-by-three grid of Friday windows photographed straight-on from the mall floor, each a single look on a flat colour plane, numbered 'No. 001' to 'No. 009' in tall serif numerals on the glass.

ips.name: THE TRIAL ROOM
ips.line: Bylined columns by Westside's own stylists, shot inside the trial room of their home store. Each column ends in a fitting you can book with that stylist.
ips.role: Help and hub: the always-on editorial voice and the main conversion path. It merges three draft IPs: The Style Collective supplies the bylines, the trial room is the set, and Style Call is the booking.
ips.precedent: Zara's The Fold-er (12 Jun 2026) runs four bylined columns (Leandra Medine, Arielle Charnas, Manon De Velder, Laura Roso Vidrequin) inside zara.com and the app. Each uses the author's own photos with a shop link under every image. Zara's Nanjing flagship has a 'fit check' studio (21 Mar 2025) with brand-controlled cameras and light; it is booked through WeChat and the video goes straight to the shopper's phone.
ips.format: Each column has a 250-word essay, 6-8 portraits of real members in the store's trial room, a shoppable edit showing stock at that store, and a 30-second mirror Reel. It closes with a 'Book me at <store>' WhatsApp button for an in-store fitting or a 15-minute video Style Call.
ips.cadence: Fortnightly per columnist. Pilot with 4 columnists in 4 stores; 30-50 in year one (one per new-format store); grow toward 300 only while quality holds. Columns are collected each quarter as 'The Trial Room, Vol. 0X'.
ips.channels: A named section in the Westside app and site (the Fold-er model), WestStyleClub WhatsApp, and collab posts with the stylist's own Instagram. YNG creators re-cut columns for their own handles.
ips.cast: Westside store stylists and Style Collective members, named with their store. Their real clients (WestStyleClub members, with consent) are the sitters. One YNG creator writes a guest column per issue.
art_direction: Set: one house trial-room spec in new-format and flagship stores: a warm plaster wall in one tone, a full-length mirror and one fixed soft top light. All 311 rooms should read as the same room.
Frame: shot full-length through the half-drawn curtain or into the mirror, at 4:5 and 9:16. The curtain edge is the signature.
Camera: a fixed rig on a house phone mount at chest height, never a handheld selfie. The stylist directs and the rig shoots.
Casting: real members of any age and size, never models. Faces may be cropped at the phone for privacy.

Typography: a magazine byline ('THE TRIAL ROOM / BY <NAME>, WESTSIDE <STORE>, <CITY>'), the essay in sentence case and product names in small capitals. Prices appear only in the shop edit, never on the portrait.
Colour: a neutral daylight grade, so the clothes carry the only colour.
ips.store_hook: Every column is datelined to one store and ends in 'Book a fitting with <stylist> at <store>'. The stylist pulls the column's pieces in the member's size and holds a trial room for 30 minutes.
ips.kpi: Fittings and Style Calls booked per store, and the show-up rate. Member-attributed bills from booked fittings (average transaction value against the store average). Column reads and saves in the app.
episode_examples: The Trial Room No. 01: 'Three Kurtas, One Office Week' by <stylist>, Westside <store>, Pune
The Trial Room No. 07: 'The 8:12 Virar Fast: Dressing for a Monsoon Commute'
The Trial Room No. 12: 'First Week of College: Five Looks from One Nuon Rail'
ips.hero_visual: A half-drawn trial-room curtain frames a woman in a full-length mirror trying an E.T.A. blazer over a Utsa kurta, with the small credit line 'THE TRIAL ROOM / BY <STYLIST>, WESTSIDE <STORE>, PUNE'.

ips.name: STORE No.
ips.line: Every new Westside opens as a numbered premiere. The store number is the edition, the city sets a small capsule, and the first evening is by guest list.
ips.role: Moment at scale and the pilot vehicle. Westside opens 50-100 stores a year and its growth comes from new stores, so this property grows with the business. It replaces First Look.
ips.precedent: Zara premieres each big drop in one room before rolling it out. Examples: the 50 Creators pop-up at 40 avenue George V (2-5 Oct 2025, curated by Sarah Andelman, with talks and a café), the Galliano Re{form} installation booked by appointment on zara.com, and Bad Bunny's hometown preview at Plaza Las Americas (16 May 2026). The 50 Years, 50 Icons film tied many faces to the first store to build a founding myth.
ips.format:
A 3-day premiere run from a fixed kit by a four-person travelling crew.
- Day 1: a guest-list evening for top WestStyleClub members in the store's pin codes, local FRONT ROW culture-shapers and city press.
- Day 2: a 6am Wesness run from the store door, then a 45-minute app livestream hosted in the store.
- Day 3: open to the public.
Around it: a 12-piece city capsule tagged with the store number, one commissioned local-artist object in the window, and portraits of the first 30 customers.
ips.cadence: Every opening, 50-100 a year, numbered by Westside's own store count. 311 stores were open on 30 Sep 2026, so the next is No. 312.
ips.channels: A countdown on the hoarding; WestStyleClub WhatsApp to members in the catchment; geo-paid social within 5 km; the local YNG and Style Collective cohort on their own handles within 72 hours; city press and radio; one frame on the national grid.
ips.cast: The first 30 customers, store staff introduced by name, a local cohort of 3-5 YNG creators and stylists, one local FRONT ROW culture-shaper as host, and a local artist or craft cluster.
art_direction: The store number is the logo of the week: 'No. 312' in the house serif on the hoarding, invitation, bag sticker and first post, with the city name in its own script beneath.
The hoarding is the teaser: plain uppercase lines only ('No. 312. OPENS FRIDAY. HYDERABAD.'), with no renders and no faces.

Portraits of the first 30 customers are shot at the entrance on a seamless backdrop in the current issue colour, with the same lens, height and distance at every opening, so 100 openings build one archive.
One local object, not decoration: a single commissioned piece in the window (Bidri inlay in Hyderabad, cane and bamboo in Guwahati). No balloon arches or ribbon.
Film: one locked-off 60-second take of the shutter rising on opening morning.
ips.store_hook: The property is the store itself. Members book the guest list on WhatsApp by pin code, and the city capsule sells only in that store for 14 days. Each first-30 portrait is printed and handed over when the sitter comes back for it a week later, which builds a second visit into the format.
ips.kpi: Footfall in opening week and at day 30, against plan and against the last 10 openings without the format. New WestStyleClub sign-ups per opening. 30-day repeat-visit rate, measured by portrait collection.
episode_examples: Store No. 312, Hyderabad: 'Bidri'
Store No. 325, Guwahati: 'Eri' (an eri-silk city capsule)
Store No. 350, Gurugram: 'The First Thirty'
ips.hero_visual: A shuttered storefront at dawn with 'No. 312' painted in tall serif numerals across the shutter, thirty people waiting in a single line, and one Bidri-inlaid sculpture visible through the glass.

ips.name: ROSHNI
ips.line: Every Diwali, one named Indian artist lights Westside: a numbered capsule, one large light sculpture in a single flagship, and a scaled light object in every window.
ips.role: Annual hero moment. It claims the festive calendar that Zara entered once in India and did not return to.
ips.precedent: Zara x Jayesh Sachdev 'Reverie' (15 Oct 2024) was Zara's first India collaboration: a Diwali capsule of tees, sweatshirts, totes and patchouli candles. It was anchored by a 10-foot tiger sculpture at Phoenix Palladium, Mumbai, with corners in Delhi, Bengaluru, Pune and Gurugram. No 2025 or 2026 sequel was found. The year-two variant borrows from Zara's 50 Creators, in which 50 cultural figures each made one object sold for charity.
ips.format: A 30-40 piece capsule across Utsa, Vark and home (kurtas, sarees, a candle, a brass diya, a gift box), designed with the artist. One 3-4 metre light sculpture in a metro flagship, a scaled light object for every window bay, a 90-second artist film, and a numbered edition card sewn or packed into every piece.
ips.cadence: Annual. Opens the Saturday before Dhanteras and runs 21 days. Numbered ROSHNI 01, 02... Edition 01 is realistic for Diwali 2027, given lead times.
ips.channels: 311 windows, app and site home, Westside Instagram, design and art press as well as fashion press, WestStyleClub early access, and the flagship installation.
ips.cast: The artist, named and quoted, with their name set as large as Westside's. The craft cluster that made the objects, credited by name. One three-generation family for the campaign.
art_direction: Light is the only decoration. No marigold strings, rangoli stickers or firecracker graphics: one object, one light source.
Shoot after dark, lit only by the sculpture and real diyas: deep shadow, warm skin, no fill flash.
The artist sets three colours each year (e.g. lamp-black, brass, ivory), never the default festive red and gold.
Typography: ROSHNI in the house serif with रोशनी in Devanagari at equal size, then 'EDITION 01 / <ARTIST>'.
Casting: three generations of one family in a single frame, with natural make-up by Studiowest and no festive glam.
ips.store_hook: The full-size sculpture stands in one named flagship for 21 days, with free 15-minute evening viewings booked on WhatsApp. Every other store gets the scaled light object in its window bay. The capsule sells in stores for seven days before it is released to the app.
ips.kpi: Flagship footfall and viewing bookings over the 21 days. Capsule sell-through by day 10, per store. Festive-period footfall per store against last Diwali. Design and art press pick-ups.
episode_examples: ROSHNI 01: 'Akash Kandil' (a three-metre Maharashtrian sky lantern in paper and brass)
ROSHNI 02: '30 Diyas' (30 FRONT ROW culture-shapers each design one diya, sold numbered for a named craft cause)
ROSHNI 03: 'Lamp-black'
ips.hero_visual: A three-metre paper-and-brass akash kandil glows above a three-generation family dressed in ivory Utsa, lit only by the lantern, with 'ROSHNI / रोशनी, EDITION 01' set small in one corner.

ips.name: THE SERIAL
ips.line: A six-episode wedding-season drama, one function per episode, premiered every Sunday at 9pm in the Westside app. Every outfit is on a rail in store the next morning.
ips.role: Annual long-form hero. Westside has made no festive or wedding film in the last year; this one is built as a recognisable Indian genre rather than an ad.
ips.precedent: Willy Chavarria's 'Vatisimo' for Zara (26 Mar 2026) was a telenovela-style short film he co-directed with Glen Luchford. 'Le Dîner' (11 Dec 2025) was a roughly 15-minute Christmas film premiered at 20:00 inside the Zara app and online, before cut-downs went to social.
ips.format: Six 6-8 minute episodes (Roka, Mehendi, Sangeet, Haldi, Phere, Vidaai), shot like a Hindi family serial by a cinema crew, each ending on a cliffhanger. A 40-minute cut for the finale. 10-15 single-character clips per episode. A 'shop the episode' page listing stock by store.
ips.cadence: Annual, weekly through wedding season (mid-November to late December), premiering Sundays at 21:00 IST. Numbered Season 01, 02...
ips.channels: Premiere in the Westside app and on the site; a WestStyleClub WhatsApp alert for each episode; full episodes on YouTube 24 hours later; clips on Reels and Shorts through YNG creators; the finale as a ticketed screening in one flagship.
ips.cast: A three-generation family of 12: two FRONT ROW culture-shapers in the lead roles, actors from Hindi independent film and theatre, and real Westside staff as the recurring shop assistants. Directed by a director from Indian independent cinema; beauty by Studiowest.
art_direction: Play the serial straight, not as parody: locked-off frames and long takes, with one dramatic whip-zoom allowed per episode.
One colour per episode, taken from the function: mehendi green, sangeet indigo, haldi yellow, sindoor red for the phere, ivory for the vidaai. The grade, set and wardrobe follow it.
A recurring set in every episode: a Westside trial room where the family argues about outfits.
Casting: real Indian ages and bodies. The aunties are written as people, not jokes.
Title cards in the house serif with a Devanagari subtitle ('EPISODE 04 / HALDI / हल्दी'), and full film credits at the end.
No price, logo bug or call to action inside the film. Commerce lives only on the episode page.
ips.store_hook: Every Monday a 'shop the episode' rail appears in the trial-room zone of every store. The WhatsApp link on the episode page books a fitting for the exact look at the member's nearest store. The finale screens as a ticketed night in one flagship.
ips.kpi: Episode completion rate in the app. Episode-linked fitting bookings and member-attributed bills, per store per week. Wedding-season sell-through of Utsa, Vark and E.T.A. against last season.
episode_examples: Season 01, Ep. 01 'Roka: Who Wears Red First'
Season 01, Ep. 03 'Sangeet: The Rehearsal Nobody Came To'
Season 01, Ep. 06 'Vidaai: The Car Won't Start'
ips.hero_visual: A family of twelve crowds in and around a single Westside trial room under haldi-yellow light, mid-argument, framed like a TV-serial still with 'THE SERIAL / EPISODE 04 / HALDI / हल्दी' set small along the bottom.

ips.name: RE-EDITION
ips.line: Twice a year, an Indian designer reworks Westside's own archive into a numbered volume, sold first by appointment in one new store.
ips.role: Scarcity moment for the quiet months (March and August). It draws newness from Westside's own history and gives people a reason to visit a named store outside the festive peaks.
ips.precedent: In Re{form} Zara by John Galliano, Galliano deconstructs garments from Zara's past seasons into numbered volumes over two years. Vol. 1 has 157 items at $29.99-999.99 and went on sale on 1 Oct 2026. It was shown by appointment in a Marais hôtel particulier, booked through zara.com, and a neckerchief sold out by 09:45 on launch day. Target's 2019 20th Anniversary archive collection is a second precedent, but it comes from memory and is unverified.
ips.format: A 25-40 piece volume built from archive prints, silhouettes and deadstock (Bombay Paisley prints, early Utsa kurtas, E.T.A. and KALA tailoring). A black-and-white studio portrait campaign by the house photographer. A digital archive book pairing each original with its rework. A by-appointment room in one new store for the first three days.
ips.cadence: Twice a year: Vol. 01 in March, Vol. 02 in August. Each designer partnership runs two years (four volumes), then a new designer takes over.
ips.channels: One store by WhatsApp appointment, then 20 stores and the app from day four. Fashion press. FRONT ROW seeding: two culture-shapers wear pieces in public 4-6 weeks before the reveal.
ips.cast: The designer (from FRONT ROW, or a YNG/NIFT alumnus), credited as creative director of the volume. 6-8 sitters, one for each decade of age from the 20s to the 70s. The original Westside designers and pattern-makers, credited where known.
art_direction: Studio portraits on a grey seamless backdrop, in black and white for the campaign. Colour appears only on product pages.
Show the source: every reworked piece is photographed beside its archive original, with the label and year.
Typography: 'RE-EDITION / VOL. 01 / <DESIGNER>' in uppercase sans, with archive years in the house serif.
Archive colours as found: no seasonal palette, no festive props.
Prices stay inside Westside's normal range. Scarcity comes from limited quantities and access, not a premium tier.
ips.store_hook: Each volume sells only in one named new store for three days, by 30-minute WhatsApp appointment, with the archive originals hung on a single rail beside the reworks. It reaches 20 stores and the app on day four.
ips.kpi: Appointments booked and kept. Time to first sell-out. Footfall at the premiere store against its opening plan. Share of buyers who are new WestStyleClub members. Press pick-ups.

RE-EDITION VOL. 02: 'E.T.A., Unpicked' (archive tailoring taken apart and recut)
RE-EDITION VOL. 03: 'The First Utsa Kurtas'
ips.hero_visual: A black-and-white studio portrait of a woman in a reworked Bombay Paisley shirt-dress, with the original printed shirt hanging on a rail beside her and 'RE-EDITION / VOL. 01' set small beneath.

slates.lens: Target lens, accessible style authority. The question was what Westside's Target Style and Club Target are. Westside's Target Style is SEEN: a dedicated style channel (@seenatwestside, a SEEN tab in the Westside app and a WestStyleClub WhatsApp channel). It runs @TargetStyle's three formats to Zara's art-direction standard: trend edits become The Window, stylist tips become The Trial Room and street style becomes Seen In. Westside's Club Target is The Regulars, a tiered creator ladder built on WestStyleClub IDs and home stores. Creators earn rewards for store bills and visits, not clicks. Target's 'owned brands, each with a personality' idea becomes Editions. Culture and humour become Just Looking. Its phrase 'bas dekh rahe hain' ('just looking') is Westside's 'Target run': it names the store trip, not a product. Caveat: every Target precedent comes from the brief or model memory. No Target source was reachable in this research, so there are no Target URLs. Verify them before they go in the deck. All Zara precedents carry the source URLs from the research.
slates.architecture:
Two surfaces, one house look.

(1) The brand handle @westside stays a quiet magazine and carries the hero moments: Editions (one label a month), The Function (once a year) and First Look (every opening).

(2) The new style channel @seenatwestside, with the app's SEEN tab and the WestStyleClub WhatsApp channel, is the Target Style equivalent. It runs a fixed weekly rhythm so people learn when to look: Monday Just Looking, Wednesday The Trial Room, Friday The Window, Sunday Seen In.

The help layer sits inside the content. Style Call is folded into The Trial Room: every episode ends in a WhatsApp booking with that stylist in that store.

The Regulars is the volume engine and the Club Target equivalent. Style Collective, YNG, Wesness run captains and FRONT ROW fold into one ladder with one ID. The 72-hour Burst is folded in as the distribution rule for every hero moment: local Regulars, 150-200 city meme and news pages, PR, and geo-paid ads within 5-8 km of the named store.

House rules across all eight properties:
- One fixed photographer, stylist and art director, held for four seasons and credited on every post.
- Everything numbered (Window No. 047, Trial Room No. 012, First Look No. 087).
- Three named colours per issue.
- No price or offer on hero assets; offers stay in CRM and WhatsApp.
- Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts and WhatsApp only (TikTok is banned in India).
- One sign-off on every asset: 'Seen at Westside, <store>, <city>'.

Owned language: 'Seen at Westside', 'bas dekh rahe hain' (Just Looking) and 'the Westside run' (Wesness Saturday runs that start and end at a store).

KPI spine: footfall per store, then bills per member.

Pilot: First Look No. 001 at one new store, with The Window, Seen In and The Trial Room running there for eight weeks against matched control stores. The festive-drop alternative is The Function. The Oct-Nov 2026 festive window is too close to make six episodes, so Season 1 targets the Jan-Feb 2027 wedding dates and then runs every year from Dhanteras.

Store names in the titles below are illustrative; lock them to Westside's store list.

slates.lens: FOOTFALL: every property is designed backwards from a visit to a named store and measured per store. The cast is local stylists, store teams and members. Booking runs on WhatsApp. The big moments are store openings, festive and weddings. Wesness, YNG and FRONT ROW are plugged in. It still has to look Zara-grade.
slates.architecture:
Seen at Westside works as one magazine with 311 addresses. Three rules apply to every property.
(1) Every asset carries a dateline and a number, for example 'TRIAL ROOM No. 012 · WESTSIDE, BANJARA HILLS, HYDERABAD'.
(2) Every asset ends in one of three store actions, each sent through that store's own WhatsApp number with a property code:
- BOOK: a Style Call or a trial-room slot.
- HOLD: reserve your size at that store.
- RSVP: get on a guest list.
(3) The WestStyleClub ID is captured at the billing counter. That links post, booking, visit and bill for each store. Results are read against matched control stores and the malls' footfall counters.

LAYERS
- HERO: The Window. Every Friday, every store; it is the weekly cover.
- HUB: The Trial Room (weekly film) and Dateline (fortnightly stylist column).
- HELP: Style Call. It is the booking step that every other property ends in.
- COMMUNITY: Start Line. Wesness runs start and end at stores.
- MOMENTS: First Look (each of the 50-100 openings a year), Dehleez (Navratri to Diwali) and Five Functions (the November-February wedding season).
- Monsoon and office (June-September) and college (July-August) run as briefs inside the always-on properties.

CAST
The Style Collective is no longer a property. It becomes the one pool of cast, organised by store catchment:
- 30-50 stylists in the pilot;
- one per store (300+) at scale;
- about 1,500 once members, YNG creators and Wesness captains are included.
The ladder runs member, then YNG creator, then Style Collective stylist, then FRONT ROW. Everyone has a WestStyleClub ID and a home store. The perks happen in store: Window previews, trial-room shoot slots, preview-night invites.
Each platform has a job:
- FRONT ROW supplies hosts and the Dehleez artist.
- YNG supplies college hosts, guest columnists and portrait photographers.
- Wesness supplies Start Line.

DISTRIBUTION
The 72-hour Burst is no longer a property. It becomes the release rule for every moment: 72 hours of clipper pages, local creators, PR and geo-targeted paid media, all limited to 5-8 km around the named store.

HOUSE LOOK
- One fixed crew for at least four seasons: Umashan Naidoo as chief creative, plus one external photographer and one external stylist.
- Westside wordmark in Bodoni Moda; datelines and credits in Inter Tight capitals.
- Three named colours per season.
- One commissioned track per season, also played in store.
- Full credits on every post.
- No price or offer on hero assets. Offers stay in WhatsApp and the CRM.

PILOT
- Five Functions, Style Call and The Trial Room in one city cluster for the January-February 2027 wedding dates, against matched control stores.
- First Look at the next store opening.
- Dehleez Edition 01 for Diwali 2027.

CAVEATS
- The Zara facts come from search-result text; the pages themselves could not be opened. Check them before the deck goes out.
- The Target ideas used here (one house frame over many owned labels; selling the trip, as in 'Target run') come from memory and are unverified, so they are not cited.
- Store names in the examples are illustrative. Confirm them against Westside's store list.

ips.role: Hero, always-on. The weekly cover of the Seen at Westside 'issue': the same image goes up the same day on Instagram, the app home, the WestStyleClub WhatsApp header and in 311 physical windows. It gives people a reason to walk past the store, and then in.
ips.precedent: Zara SRPLS: numbered CLLCTN releases (CLLCTN 02 to CLLCTN 16 in about 7.5 years) under one fixed creative director (Karl Templer) and one recurring photographer (Craig McDean), which turned routine drops into a collectible run. Also Zara's practice of changing its windows with each campaign, so the window is the physical cover of the same issue as the grid and the home page.
ips.format: One look on a single mannequin, shot in the window. Assets: one 4:5 still, one 6-second 9:16 loop, one WhatsApp header crop and one A5 rail card in store with the window number, the label and a QR code to reserve your size.
ips.cadence: Weekly, Friday 10:00. The window is photographed at 07:00, before the store or mall opens. Numbered continuously from Window No. 001, 52 a year. The central visual-merchandising pack ships on Tuesday and is installed on Thursday night.
ips.channels: 311 store windows; the @westside grid (one hero store per week, rotating); Westside app and site home; WestStyleClub WhatsApp header; in-store rail card; window screens in flagships looping the 6-second film.
ips.cast: Each store's visual-merchandising lead, credited by name as 'Dressed by'; one central creative director for the series (a named Westside VM head); one fixed photographer who shoots the rotating hero store.
art_direction: One look, one mannequin, no props. The window backdrop is a single seamless field in the season's lead colour (monsoon: slate), with nothing else in the frame.
Shot straight on at mannequin eye level from the pavement or mall corridor, with the street or concourse reflection allowed in the glass, so the neighbourhood is part of the picture.
Early light before the store lights come up; a single overhead source inside the window; no gels, no retouched-away reflections.
'WINDOW No. 047' in Inter Tight capitals top left, the dateline 'WESTSIDE, KALYANI NAGAR, PUNE' bottom left, credits bottom right in 10px grey. No price, no 'NEW', no percentage off.
Each look comes from one label (E.T.A., Utsa, Wardrobe, Nuon, Bombay Paisley), rotating so the labels read as characters in one magazine. The label name sits on the rail card, not on the hero image.
ips.store_hook: The full window look, in all sizes, sits on a 'Window rail' just inside the door for seven days. Sending 'WINDOW 047' to that store's WhatsApp holds your size for 48 hours, and the QR code on the rail card does the same. WestStyleClub members get the window photo on Thursday night so they can reserve before it goes up.
ips.kpi: Per store, per week: WINDOW reservations on WhatsApp and the share collected; Window-rail sell-through within seven days compared with the rest of the floor; Friday-to-Sunday footfall against that store's weekend average, read against matched stores that install the same window a week later (a staggered test).

ips.name: The Trial Room
ips.line: A real member, a store stylist and one Westside trial room: three looks, one mirror, filmed from behind the curtain. That trial room can be booked the same week.
ips.role: Hub, always-on. A weekly video series that makes the most private place in the store its set, and shows what an app cannot do: trying clothes on with someone who knows.
ips.precedent: Zara's Nanjing flagship 'fit check' studio (opened 21 Mar 2025): several cameras, brand-controlled lighting, booked through WeChat, so shoppers make content tied to one store. Also Zara Store Mode's fitting-room booking, where the app assigns a room and the customer has five minutes to claim it.
ips.format: A 45-60 second vertical film plus a 5-frame carousel. The member arrives with a brief ('client pitch on Monday'), the stylist passes three looks through the curtain, and the member chooses one at the mirror. One permanently dressed Trial Room in each new-format store doubles as a self-shoot bay for members.
ips.cadence: Weekly, on Wednesdays, numbered (Trial Room No. 001 onwards) in seasons of 12. The brief rotates monthly: office, monsoon, college, festive, wedding guest.
ips.channels: @westside Reels and Shorts; Westside app; WestStyleClub WhatsApp (the full episode arrives with a 'book this trial room' button); screens beside the trial rooms in store.
ips.cast: Real WestStyleClub members, cast through a 'cast me' call on WhatsApp, with releases signed and fees paid; that store's Style Collective stylist; YNG creators host the college season; store staff appear as themselves.
art_direction: The curtain is the frame. Shoot from outside the trial room with the curtain half drawn: a sliver of mirror, a hand passing a hanger, the member's face. No full-length catalogue shot until the reveal.
One light: swap the trial room's ceiling light for a single warm 3200K panel and keep the mirror's own light. Grain is allowed; beauty filters are not.
Cast real members across ages, sizes and skin tones. Studiowest artists do hair and make-up, kept natural and unfinished. Never models.

Every room in the series is dressed the same way: one hook, one stool, one full-length mirror, the wall painted in the season colour, and the room number stencilled on the door ('TRIAL ROOM 4 · WESTSIDE, BANJARA HILLS').
Sound is room tone and the curtain rail; the season's commissioned track plays only on the reveal.
End card: room number and dateline in Inter Tight capitals, with member, stylist and store credited in 10px grey. No price anywhere in the film.
ips.store_hook: 'Book this trial room': message the store's WhatsApp with the episode number. The stylist pulls the three looks in your size and holds that trial room for a 30-minute slot on a day you choose, and you can bring a friend into the same slot.
ips.kpi: Per store: trial-room slots booked from episodes; share of bookings that turn up; share of booked slots that end in a bill (WestStyleClub ID); average bill of booked shoppers compared with walk-ins; members applying to be cast.

ips.name: Dateline
ips.line: A bylined column by a named Westside stylist on what their neighbourhood is actually wearing this fortnight, ending with when to find them on the shop floor.
ips.role: Hub, always-on editorial. The Style Collective's voice, published on Westside's own channels. It makes stylists into local names and gives every city its own fashion page.
ips.precedent: Zara's The Fold-er (from 12 Jun 2026): bylined columns by named writers inside zara.com and the app, illustrated with the authors' own photographs and a shop link under every image, so influencer credibility sits on Zara's own channel. Also Zara Man's named editorial series ('Selected By', 'Archive'), each with one photographer.
ips.format: A column of about 300 words with 6-8 photographs taken on the stylist's own streets and in their store. Under every photo: 'in stock at Westside [store]' and a reserve button. It closes with the stylist's hours on the floor and a Style Call link. Cut down into a 4-frame carousel and a WhatsApp card.
ips.cadence: Fortnightly per stylist. Pilot: four stylists (Mumbai, Pune, Bengaluru, Hyderabad), which is two columns a week. Scale: one stylist per city cluster, 26 columns a year each. YNG guest columns during college season (July-August).
ips.channels: Westside app and site editorial section; WestStyleClub WhatsApp, segmented by city (Pune members get Dateline: Pune); @westside carousel; a printed A4 sheet on the notice board by the trial rooms.
ips.cast: Style Collective stylists, each with a home store; YNG creators as guest columnists; locals photographed on the street with consent and credited by first name.
art_direction: Laid out like a newspaper dateline: 'DATELINE: KORAMANGALA, BENGALURU' in Inter Tight capitals, the byline underneath, then one headline word in Bodoni Moda.
The stylist shoots on a phone to a house rule: natural light only, eye level, 3:4 portrait, people rather than flat-lays, one subject per frame.
Every column names and shoots a real local place: a darshini counter, a college gate, a metro exit, an office lobby. The city is the set.
Black on white with generous margins. No stickers, emoji or price graphics; product appears as small-capital lines under each image.
The house photographer shoots each stylist's byline portrait in their store once a season, so even the byline carries the house look.
ips.store_hook: Every column ends with 'Find me on the floor at Westside [store], Saturdays 4-8pm' and a Style Call link that books that stylist. Every pictured piece shows live stock for that store with 'reserve to try'.
ips.kpi: Per stylist and store: Style Call and floor bookings from the column link; reserve-to-try holds and the share collected; bills attributed to the stylist through the WestStyleClub ID; WhatsApp read rate by city segment.

ips.name: Style Call
ips.line: A 15-minute WhatsApp video call with a stylist at your nearest Westside, who has your looks waiting in a trial room before you arrive.
ips.role: Help, always-on. The booking step that every other property ends in, and the one place where a social post becomes a dated, timed store visit with a named person waiting.
ips.precedent: Zara Try-On (from Dec 2025): an app-only tool that answers 'will it suit me', with more than 7M sessions in 43 markets by 11 Mar 2026 (Inditex). Also Zara Streaming, which Zara kept on its own app but scaled back after critics called it teleshopping. Style Call takes the lesson from the tool, not the spectacle: human, one-to-one, ending in a store slot.
ips.format: A service that also makes content. Customers book on the store's WhatsApp Business number (keyword 'STYLE', or a deep link from any post) for a 15-minute video call; the looks are pulled and a trial room held for a 30-minute slot within 72 hours. Content: a monthly 'Style Call Log' film edited from calls customers agree to share, and each stylist's weekly availability posted as a WhatsApp card.
ips.cadence: Always-on, seven days a week, with each store's slots released every Monday. One Log film a month. Evening slots added before Diwali and through the November-February wedding season.
ips.channels: Per-store WhatsApp Business numbers linked to WestStyleClub; Westside app; deep links from every property; QR codes at the store entrance and the trial rooms; an Instagram highlight called 'Book a Style Call'.
ips.cast: Style Collective stylists (30-50 across about 10 stores in the pilot, then one trained stylist per store, 300+); store managers on the evening rota; customers who agree to appear in the Log.
art_direction: The Log is a split screen: the customer's raw vertical phone video beside the stylist's view of the rail, in a white frame with the call timer visible.
The stylist is always on the shop floor, never at a desk or in front of a ring light; rails and the store's signage are behind them.
The WhatsApp card is purely typographic: the stylist's first name, the store and the next free slots in Inter Tight capitals on white, with one square portrait.
Copy reads like Zara's interface: BOOK, CALL, HOLD MY TRIAL ROOM. No emoji, no exclamation marks, no 'hurry'.
The arrival is designed too: a printed card with the customer's name on the held trial-room door, photographed so they can share it.
ips.store_hook: Every call ends with a slot, for example: 'Your trial room is held at Westside [store], Saturday 5:30pm, with Priya.' The looks are pulled in your size before you arrive, a WhatsApp reminder goes out three hours before, and the stylist meets you at the door.
ips.kpi: Per store and stylist: calls booked; share of calls that lead to a visit; share of visits that end in a bill; average bill compared with walk-ins; no-show rate; repeat bookings within 90 days. Benchmarks are set in the pilot and read against control stores without Style Call.

ips.name: Start Line
ips.line: Every Wesness run starts and ends at a Westside store, on a numbered route card, with a playlist chosen by the run captain and chai inside the store before the shutters go up.
ips.role: Community, always-on plus one annual moment. It brings the 25,000 Wesness runners through the door on Saturday mornings, and it builds an annual Wesness 10K whose kit can only be collected in stores.
ips.precedent: Zara Athleticz Speed Run: Zara's own annual Madrid 10K, certified by the Spanish athletics federation (RFEA), with about 10,000 places, branded kit and a livestream; the 2025 edition set a Spanish women's 10K record (30:59). Also Athleticz's launch playlists and its named running 'curator'.
ips.format: Weekly: a numbered route card (5K and 10K loops from the store), the run captain's playlist, a 20-second film and a 9-frame finish-line carousel. Annual: the Wesness 10K, a certified women's race in one city (Bengaluru first), with kit collected at 10-15 of that city's stores during race week.
ips.cadence: Weekly on Saturdays at 06:00 in Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad and Bengaluru, starting from a different store in each city every week. Race on one Sunday in December, with kit collection in the week before.
ips.channels: Wesness WhatsApp communities; a Strava club; @westside and Wesness Instagram; Spotify playlists; Westside app; race livestream.
ips.cast: Wesness run captains, one credited each season as the curator of routes and playlist; Wesness members; the start store's team, who open at 05:45 and run too; local women's running clubs as guests.
art_direction: Shot at first light, 05:45-06:30, in natural light only. The opening frame of every film is the store's lit front with the pack of runners in front of it.
The cast is the run itself: Wesness women of every pace and age, no athlete models. Sweat, dupattas tied as headbands and monsoon puddles stay in.
The route card is a numbered object: 'START LINE No. 024 · WESTSIDE [store] · 5.2 KM' in Inter Tight capitals with a single-line map, printed on card stock and handed out at the door.
Two colours per season (for example dawn pink and asphalt grey) across bibs, route cards and type.
Finish portraits are shot one runner per frame against the store's shutter or window, captioned with first name and time only.
ips.store_hook: Runners check in at the store door with the QR code on the route card, which links their WestStyleClub ID. From 07:00 to 08:00, before opening, there is a stretch and chai inside the store with the activewear rail and the Studiowest skincare counter open to runners. In race week, kit can only be collected in stores.
ips.kpi: Per start store: runners checked in; new WestStyleClub sign-ups among runners; bills by runners on the day and within seven days; kit-collection visits in race week; repeat runs per member.

ips.name: First Look
ips.line: Every new Westside opens as a numbered premiere: a guest-list evening for the neighbourhood the night before, one object by a local maker alone in the window, and an opening weekend that seeds every other property in that store.
ips.role: Moment, rolling with the 50-100 openings a year. It turns Westside's main source of growth, new stores, into content, and it recruits a new local cast (stylists, members, creators) for each store.
ips.precedent: Zara's rule of premiering in one room: Re{form} Zara by John Galliano Vol. 1 was shown by appointment, booked through zara.com, at a hôtel particulier in the Marais during Paris Fashion Week; Bad Bunny's collection previewed at a hometown pop-up in Plaza Las Américas, Puerto Rico (16 May 2026), before the global drop.
ips.format: Preview night the evening before opening (250-400 RSVPs by WhatsApp). A 45-minute livestream on the Westside app and WhatsApp, hosted by a FRONT ROW culture-shaper from that city. An opening-weekend programme: a Start Line run from the store, the store's first Trial Room episode and its first Dateline column. A commissioned object by a local maker in the window. A 72-hour burst limited to the store's catchment.
ips.cadence: One per opening, numbered by store count (First Look No. 312, 313 and so on). New cities and new formats get the full programme; infill stores get a lighter kit: preview night, window object and burst.
ips.channels: WhatsApp invites and RSVPs; geo-targeted Instagram, YouTube and Meta paid media within 5-8 km; local clipper and city pages; local press; app livestream; mall screens.
ips.cast: The new store's own team, introduced by name; FRONT ROW culture-shapers and New Faces from that city; the local YNG cohort; WestStyleClub members invited by postcode; one local maker; the city's Wesness chapter.
art_direction: The store is shot empty and fully lit the night before, as one wide, dead-symmetrical frame from the entrance. That image is the cover for the opening.
Every team member gets a magazine-style portrait against the store's own wall, with name and role in capitals. Together they form the store's 'masthead' on its WhatsApp card.
One commissioned local object stands alone in the window for the opening month, with no product beside it: a Sualkuchi muga-silk panel in Guwahati, bidri in Hyderabad, kantha in Kolkata.
The invitation is a letterpress card with the store number and address, mirrored exactly in the WhatsApp invite.
The livestream is directed like a short film: fixed cameras, one host, no presenter desk, no countdown graphics.
Each opening takes its palette from the city (Guwahati: tea green, muga gold, river grey) across the invite, window and film.
ips.store_hook: Neighbours RSVP on WhatsApp for the preview night. Members in the catchment can book 'first hour' trial-room slots over the opening weekend. Every guest leaves with a numbered card that brings them back within 30 days for a first Style Call with the store's stylist.
ips.kpi: Per new store: footfall in the opening week and at day 30 against the new-store benchmark for its city tier; new WestStyleClub members in the catchment; share of RSVPs who attend; return visits within 30 days; first-month sales against plan.

ips.name: Dehleez
ips.line: Dehleez is Hindi-Urdu for threshold. Every Diwali one Indian artist designs the threshold of every Westside store, and families book a free portrait standing on it in their festive best.
ips.role: Moment, the annual festive tentpole (about four weeks, Navratri to Bhai Dooj). It is Westside's missing festive campaign, built as an annual tradition of the kind Zara started with Reverie and then dropped.
ips.precedent: Zara x Jayesh Sachdev 'Reverie' (15 Oct 2024): Zara's first India collaboration, a Diwali artist capsule anchored by a 10-ft tiger sculpture at Phoenix Palladium in Mumbai, with display corners in four more cities. No 2025 sequel was found. Also '50 Years, 50 Icons': one idea, many faces, cut into one clip per face.
ips.cadence: Annual: the artist is announced in August, portrait slots open three weeks before Diwali, and the run lasts from Navratri to Bhai Dooj. Edition 01 for Diwali 2027.
ips.channels: 311 store thresholds; WhatsApp portrait booking and delivery; the film and 30 family clips on @westside; cuts in Hindi, Marathi, Telugu, Kannada, Bengali and Assamese; outdoor ads near flagships; art and design press.
ips.cast: One artist a year, drawn from FRONT ROW's culture-shapers or a living craft tradition; 30 WestStyleClub families across generations and regions, cast on WhatsApp; store teams as portrait crew, trained by the house photographer; YNG photographers in the 50 portrait stores.
art_direction: The threshold is the only decoration: one motif in three colours (for example marigold, kohl and ivory). No fairy-light clutter and no 'Diwali Sale' banners anywhere near the hero image.
Portraits are formal and frontal: the family stands on the motif, shot from slightly above so the floor design reads, in the manner of an old studio photograph.
One soft key light at 2700K, and one real lit diya in each family's hands.
The cast is the news: grandparents to babies, every region, every body. Families style themselves from the capsule with the store stylists.
'DEHLEEZ EDITION 01' in Bodoni Moda, with the artist's name and the store dateline in Inter Tight capitals. The print carries only the family name and the store.
One commissioned track, a reworked aarti or folk melody, used in the film, in stores and on every Reel.
ips.store_hook: A free 10-minute family portrait at your store's Dehleez, booked on WhatsApp, with a Studiowest touch-up before the photo. Families arrive dressed (often from the capsule, styled in store), leave with a printed portrait and get the file on WhatsApp within 24 hours. The five flagship sculptures are destinations to visit and photograph.
ips.kpi: Per store: portrait slots booked and attended; average family group size; bills from portrait families on the day; festive-period footfall against last Diwali in like-for-like stores; capsule sell-through; social posts geotagged to the store.

ips.name: Five Functions
ips.line: Bring your shaadi card to any Westside and a stylist plans your haldi, mehendi, sangeet, wedding and reception looks in one session. A five-episode wedding-video series follows one real guest doing exactly that.
ips.role: Moment, the wedding season (November to February). The season's sales driver without a discount: it turns the wedding invitation in every Indian home into a ticket into the store. It is the first pilot.
ips.precedent: Zara's genre films premiered on its own channels: 'Le Dîner' (11 Dec 2025), a 15-minute Christmas film premiered at 20:00 in the Zara app and then cut for social, and Willy Chavarria's telenovela 'Vatisimo' (26 Mar 2026). Also the two Kate Moss editions, each set by a real occasion (party season, then festival season).
ips.format: Five 3-4 minute episodes in the language of an Indian wedding video, one real guest and one function per episode, each guest styled in a named store. They premiere one a night at 21:00 in the WestStyleClub WhatsApp channel and the app, then are cut for social. In stores: 45-minute 'Bring the Card' sessions, booked on WhatsApp or as a walk-in.
ips.cadence: Episodes released over one week before the first peak wedding dates of the season (dates checked each year). 'Bring the Card' runs throughout November to February. One numbered edition a year; the pilot is the January-February 2027 dates in one city cluster.
ips.channels: WestStyleClub WhatsApp channel and app premiere; @westside and YouTube; family WhatsApp groups via shareable episode links; regional-language cuts; wedding planners and venues in the pilot city.
ips.cast: Real wedding guests from WestStyleClub (the cousin flying in, the groom's college friend, the mausi); FRONT ROW's New Faces in supporting roles; store stylists as themselves; the store's alterations tailor.
art_direction: Each episode borrows one wedding-video device (the slow-motion entrance, the family line-up, the varmala lift) and shoots it with cinema restraint. No drones, lens flares or filters, and nothing that mocks the family.
Each function has a locked colour: haldi yellow, mehendi green, sangeet midnight, wedding red, reception ivory. Costume, set and title cards follow it.
Real venues at the real hour of the function (a Pune lawn, a Hyderabad function hall, a Kolkata rooftop), lit only by the venue's own tungsten and string lights.
Cast across communities and budgets: a Marwari sangeet, a Telugu haldi, a Bengali reception. Menswear (E.T.A., KALA by E.T.A.) gets equal screen time.
Every episode opens on the same shot: hands opening a real invitation card. Title cards are in Bodoni Moda, for example 'EPISODE 03 · SANGEET'.
No prices and no wedding-sale graphics. Every episode closes on the dateline of the store where the guest was styled.
ips.store_hook: Bring the Card: show your wedding invitation, printed or on WhatsApp, at any Westside, or book ahead. A stylist plans all five functions in one 45-minute session, holds the looks in a trial room and books alterations with a collection date, which builds in a second visit.
ips.kpi: Per store: Bring the Card sessions booked and walk-ins; baskets covering several functions (items per bill, share of bills above a set value); return visits to collect alterations; wedding-season footfall against last season in like-for-like stores; episode completion rate on WhatsApp.
